source.text: Ἰούδας Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος, ἀδελφὸς δὲ Ἰακώβου, τοῖς ἐν θεῷ πατρὶ ἠγαπημένοις καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ τετηρημένοις κλητοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: Jude, of Jesus Christ slave, brother but of James, to the [ones] in God [the] Father having been loved and for Jesus Christ having been kept, called;

en.L: Jude, a slave of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and brother of James, to the called, loved in God [the] Father and kept for Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: From Jude, a servant of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and a brother of James, to those who have been called, who are loved by God the Father and kept safe for Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: This letter is from Jude. I am a servant of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and I am a brother of James. I am writing to you whom God has called. God the Father loves you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is keeping you safe for Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Judas, esclavo de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y hermano de Santiago, a los llamados, amados en Dios Padre y guardados para {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: De Judas, siervo de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y hermano de Santiago, a los que han sido llamados, amados por Dios Padre y guardados a salvo para {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Esta carta es de Judas. Soy siervo de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y hermano de Santiago. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} escribo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a quienes Dios ha llamado. Dios Padre {{plural_you:los|os}} ama, y {{plural_you:los|os}} guarda a salvo para {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Yuda, mtumwa wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} na ndugu yake Yakobo, kwa walioitwa, waliopendwa katika Mungu Baba na kulindwa kwa ajili ya Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Yuda, mtumishi wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} na ndugu yake Yakobo, kwa wale walioitwa, wanaopendwa na Mungu Baba na kulindwa salama kwa ajili ya Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Yuda. Mimi ni mtumishi wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na ni ndugu yake Yakobo. Ninawaandikia ninyi ambao Mungu amewaita. Mungu Baba anawapenda, na anawalinda salama kwa ajili ya Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

fr.L: Jude, esclave de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} et frère de Jacques, à ceux qui sont appelés, aimés en Dieu le Père et gardés pour Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} :
fr.B: De la part de Jude, serviteur de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} et frère de Jacques, à ceux qui ont été appelés, qui sont aimés par Dieu le Père et gardés en sûreté pour Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Jude. Je suis serviteur de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, et je suis frère de Jacques. Je vous écris, à vous que Dieu a appelés. Dieu le Père vous aime, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous garde en sûreté pour Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

ko.L: 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 종이요 야고보의 형제인 유다가, 부르심을 받은 사람들, 곧 하나님 아버지 안에서 사랑을 받고 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 위하여 지키심을 받는 사람들에게 [편지합니다].
ko.B: 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 종이며 야고보의 형제인 유다가, 부르심을 받은 사람들, 곧 하나님 아버지께 사랑을 받고 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 위해 안전하게 지켜지는 여러분에게 이 편지를 씁니다.
ko.R: 이 편지는 유다가 보냅니다. 나는 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 종이고, 야고보의 형제입니다. 나는 하나님께서 부르신 여러분에게 이 편지를 씁니다. 하나님 아버지께서는 여러분을 사랑하시고, 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 위해 여러분을 안전하게 지키고 계십니다.

vi.L: Giu-đe, nô lệ của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} và là em của Gia-cơ, gửi đến những người được kêu gọi, được yêu thương trong Đức Chúa Trời là Cha, và được gìn giữ cho Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Giu-đe, đầy tớ của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} và là em của Gia-cơ, kính gửi những người đã được kêu gọi, được Đức Chúa Trời là Cha yêu thương, và được gìn giữ an toàn cho Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Thư này của Giu-đe. Tôi là đầy tớ của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, và là em của Gia-cơ. Tôi viết cho anh chị em là những người Đức Chúa Trời đã kêu gọi. Đức Chúa Trời là Cha yêu thương anh chị em, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang gìn giữ anh chị em an toàn cho Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.

pt.L: Judas, escravo de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} e irmão de Tiago, aos chamados, amados em Deus Pai e guardados para Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.B: De Judas, servo de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} e irmão de Tiago, aos que foram chamados, que são amados por Deus Pai e guardados em segurança para Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.R: Esta carta é de Judas. Sou servo de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} e irmão de Tiago. Escrevo a vocês, a quem Deus chamou. Deus Pai ama vocês, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} está guardando vocês em segurança para Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.

am.L: የኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ባሪያና የያዕቆብ ወንድም ይሁዳ፣ በእግዚአብሔር አብ ለተወደዱና ለኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ለተጠበቁ ለተጠሩት፦
am.B: ከኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ባሪያና ከያዕቆብ ወንድም ከይሁዳ፣ ለተጠሩት፣ በእግዚአብሔር አብ ለተወደዱና ለኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ተጠብቀው ላሉት።
am.R: ይህ ደብዳቤ ከይሁዳ ነው። እኔ የኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ባሪያ ነኝ፤ የያዕቆብም ወንድም ነኝ። የምጽፈው እግዚአብሔር ለጠራችሁ ለእናንተ ነው። እግዚአብሔር አብ ይወዳችኋል፤ ለኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} እንድትደርሱም በሰላም ይጠብቃችኋል።

decisions.choice: Jude: most likely the brother of James, the leader of the Jerusalem church, and so also a brother of Jesus
alternatives: the apostle called Judas of James (Luke 6:16; Acts 1:13)
decisions.reason: The Greek name is Ἰούδας, the same name as Judas Iscariot and as Judah in the Old Testament. Matthew 13:55 and Mark 6:3 name a James and a Judas among the brothers of Jesus, and a James called the Lord's brother led the church in Jerusalem (Acts 15:13; 21:18; Galatians 1:19; 2:9). A writer who needed to say no more than "brother of James" was most likely pointing to that well-known James, which would make Jude a brother of Jesus as well. He does not claim that tie: he calls himself a slave of Jesus Christ. The New Testament names other men called Judas, among them an apostle, "Judas of James" (Luke 6:16), but Jude does not call himself an apostle and speaks of the apostles as others (verse 17).

decisions.choice: slave: someone owned by a master and wholly at his service
decisions.reason: δοῦλος is the ordinary word for a slave, a person who belongs to another. To call oneself a slave of Jesus Christ is to say that one belongs to him and serves him alone, as Paul, James and Peter also say of themselves (Romans 1:1; James 1:1; 2 Peter 1:1). Verse 4 calls Jesus Christ "our only Master", the word for a slave's owner.

decisions.choice: the called: the readers, described as loved and kept
decisions.reason: The last word, κλητοῖς, "called", is the word the article τοῖς belongs to; "loved" and "kept" are perfect participles that describe the called. The perfect tense speaks of a state that began in the past and continues: loved and still loved, kept and still kept. God's calling, love and keeping frame the letter, here and again in verses 21 and 24.

decisions.choice: loved in God the Father: loved by God and held within his love
alternatives: loved in the sphere of God the Father, as people who belong to him
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual, with "in" rather than "by". It most likely means that they are loved by God and remain within that love; verse 21 tells them to keep themselves in God's love.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "loved"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ἠγαπημένοις, "having been loved", the reading of the oldest manuscripts. Many later manuscripts read a word meaning "sanctified", and the King James Version follows them ("sanctified by God the Father"). "Loved in God" is an unusual phrase, and a copyist may have changed it to the more familiar "sanctified" (compare 1 Corinthians 1:2). Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: kept for Jesus Christ: guarded by God for the day when Jesus Christ comes
decisions.reason: Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ has no preposition. The dative case most naturally means "for" here (kept for him); it can also mean "by" (kept by him). The passive points to God as the one who keeps, the one who "is able to guard you" (verse 24). The verb τηρέω runs through the letter: the angels did not keep their position and are kept for judgment (verse 6), darkness is kept for the false teachers (verse 13), and the readers are told to keep themselves in God's love (verse 21).

decisions.choice: Jude
decisions.reason: English Bibles have long called the writer of this letter Jude, which keeps him distinct from Judas Iscariot. In Greek the two names are the same (m1).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Christ is the Greek for Messiah, the anointed king Israel was waiting for; the reader's setting chooses which word is shown.

decisions.choice: kept safe (B, R); whom God has called; God the Father ... is keeping you safe (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "kept safe", since "kept" alone could suggest being held back. Readable names God as the one who calls and keeps, as the passive voice implies (m6; compare verse 24).

decisions.choice: Judas; hermano de Santiago
decisions.reason: Spanish Bibles call the writer and his letter "Judas", the same form as Judas Iscariot, just as the Greek uses one name for both (meaning decision m1); Spanish has no separate form like English "Jude". His brother is "Santiago", the Spanish name of the Lord's brother in Galatians and of the author of James.

decisions.choice: siervo
decisions.reason: "Siervo" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "esclavo".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As in Romans and 2 Peter, the default is the usual Spanish form of the name, "Jesucristo"; the alternative separates name and title. Where a comma must follow the alternative, it sits inside the span.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Jude writes to his readers in the plural throughout the letter. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). In this verse only Readable addresses the readers directly.

decisions.choice: Yuda; ndugu yake Yakobo
decisions.reason: Swahili calls the writer "Yuda", the same name as Judas Iscariot and as Judah, just as the Greek does (m1). His brother is "Yakobo", the Swahili name of the Lord's brother in Galatians and of the author of James.

decisions.choice: mtumishi
decisions.reason: "Mtumishi" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "mtumwa".

decisions.choice: anawalinda, no span
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God and Christ inside the verb ("anawapenda", "anawalinda"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns and possessives, as in Romans and 2 Peter. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English.

decisions.choice: Jude; Jacques
decisions.reason: French, like English, has long called the writer "Jude", which keeps him apart from Judas Iscariot, though the Greek name is the same (m1). "Jacques" is the usual French form of James.

decisions.choice: esclave (L); serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets out for the Greek word: Literal keeps "esclave", and the meaning decision (m2) records that he was owned; Balanced and Readable say "serviteur".

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level, the stories of verses 5-11 and 14 included (for the whole letter); Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L), Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} (B, R)
alternatives: passé simple at Balanced for the stories
decisions.reason: Jude is a letter: he reminds the readers of what they know, and French uses the passé composé for that, as in Colossians and Ephesians. The title setting follows the style guide.

decisions.choice: the letter in 합쇼체 at every level, with "여러분" for the readers and "나" for Jude; no deity_pronoun spans (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean of the other letters: the formal style of a letter read to the church. Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for God and Christ is carried by -시-, 께서 and "그분".

decisions.choice: "유다", "야고보"; "종" for the slave at every level; "형제" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "유다" is the established Protestant form, as for the Jude of Matthew 13:55. "종" as in the Korean of James and 2 Peter: owned by a master and wholly at his service (meaning decision, footnoted). Jude is the brother of one particular man (meaning decision), so "형제" takes no span.

decisions.choice: "예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 위하여 지키심을 받는" (L); "안전하게 지켜지는" (B); "지키고 계십니다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "kept for Jesus Christ" as guarded by God for the day when Jesus Christ comes, and footnotes it. Korean "위하여" follows the meaning decision; Literal uses the honorific passive "지키심을 받다", which implies God as the keeper.

decisions.choice: "Giu-đe", "em của Gia-cơ"; "nô lệ" (L), "đầy tớ" (B, R) for doulos; "tôi" and "anh chị em" through the letter
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say whether a brother is older or younger. Jude is most likely the brother of James, the leader of the Jerusalem church (m1), who is named first among the brothers of Jesus (Mark 6:3), so Jude is "em". "Giu-đe" keeps him apart from Judas Iscariot ("Giu-đa"), as the English keeps "Jude". "Nô lệ" and "đầy tớ" follow James 1:1, and the forms of address follow James and 1 Peter.

decisions.choice: Judas; Tiago
decisions.reason: Portuguese has no separate form like the English "Jude": the writer of this letter has always been "Judas" in Portuguese ("a Carta de Judas"). "Irmão de Tiago" in the same line keeps him distinct from Judas Iscariotes (m1). He is not identified with the apostle Judas Tadeu, which the text does not say.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: the pronouns for God and Christ in this letter are written once
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout the letter.

decisions.choice: ይሁዳ (Jude), ያዕቆብ (James); ባሪያ (slave) at every level, where the English Balanced and Readable say "servant"
decisions.reason: "ይሁዳ" is the Amharic Bible form of the name, the same as for Judas; the context and "brother of James" keep this Jude apart (meaning decision m1). As in Romans 1:1 and 2 Peter 1:1, "ባሪያ" is kept for slave of Christ at every level: one owned by a master and wholly at his service (m2), which "አገልጋይ" would weaken to service only.

source.text: ἔλεος ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ ἀγάπη πληθυνθείη.

records.literal_gloss: Mercy to you and peace and love may it be multiplied.

en.L: Mercy to you and peace and love be multiplied.
en.B: May mercy, peace, and love be yours in ever greater measure.
en.R: I pray that you will have more and more mercy, peace, and love.

es.L: Misericordia, y paz, y amor {{plural_you:les|os}} sean multiplicados.
es.B: Que la misericordia, la paz y el amor {{plural_you:les|os}} sean dados en abundancia cada vez mayor.
es.R: Oro para que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} cada vez más misericordia, paz y amor.

sw.L: Rehema kwenu, na amani, na upendo viongezwe.
sw.B: Rehema, amani na upendo viwe vyenu kwa wingi zaidi na zaidi.
sw.R: Ninaomba mpate rehema, amani na upendo zaidi na zaidi.

fr.L: Miséricorde, paix et amour vous soient multipliés.
fr.B: Que la miséricorde, la paix et l’amour vous soient donnés toujours plus abondamment.
fr.R: Je prie pour que vous ayez toujours plus de miséricorde, de paix et d’amour.

ko.L: 긍휼과 평안과 사랑이 여러분에게 더욱 넘치기를 [빕니다].
ko.B: 긍휼과 평안과 사랑이 여러분에게 더욱 풍성하기를 빕니다.
ko.R: 여러분이 긍휼과 평안과 사랑을 더욱더 많이 누리기를 기도합니다.

vi.L: Nguyện lòng thương xót, bình an và tình yêu thương được gia tăng cho anh chị em.
vi.B: Nguyện lòng thương xót, bình an và tình yêu thương ngày càng gia tăng cho anh chị em.
vi.R: Tôi cầu xin cho anh chị em ngày càng có thêm lòng thương xót, bình an và tình yêu thương.

pt.L: Misericórdia a vocês, e paz e amor sejam multiplicados.
pt.B: Que a misericórdia, a paz e o amor estejam com vocês em medida cada vez maior.
pt.R: Peço a Deus que vocês tenham cada vez mais misericórdia, paz e amor.

am.R: ምሕረት፣ ሰላምና ፍቅር ይበልጥ እየበዛላችሁ እንዲሄድ እጸልያለሁ።

decisions.choice: a prayer: may mercy, peace and love be multiplied to you
decisions.reason: πληθυνθείη is a wish (the optative mood): may they be multiplied, given in greater and greater measure. 1 Peter 1:2 and 2 Peter 1:2 open with the same wish for grace and peace.

decisions.choice: mercy, peace, love: God's compassion, the wholeness he gives, and his love
decisions.reason: Most New Testament letters greet the readers with grace and peace. Jude names three gifts instead: mercy, peace and love. Love picks up "loved" in verse 1, and mercy returns in verses 21-23. All three come from God, the one in whom the readers are loved (verse 1).

decisions.choice: May mercy, peace, and love be yours in ever greater measure (B); I pray that you will have more and more (R)
alternatives: Mercy to you and peace and love be multiplied
decisions.reason: "Be multiplied" is not how English speaks of gifts. Balanced and Readable say the same wish in current English, as 2 Peter 1:2 does.

decisions.choice: "긍휼", "평안", "사랑"
decisions.reason: The key terms of the greetings in the Korean letters (2 John 3; 1 Peter 1:2): God's compassion, the peace he gives, and his love (meaning decision).

source.text: Ἀγαπητοί, πᾶσαν σπουδὴν ποιούμενος γράφειν ὑμῖν περὶ τῆς κοινῆς ἡμῶν σωτηρίας ἀνάγκην ἔσχον γράψαι ὑμῖν παρακαλῶν ἐπαγωνίζεσθαι τῇ ἅπαξ παραδοθείσῃ τοῖς ἁγίοις πίστει.

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, all diligence making to write to you about the common of us salvation, necessity I had to write to you, urging [you] to contend for the once for all having been handed over to the saints faith.

en.L: Beloved, while making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you, urging [you] to contend for the faith that was handed over once for all to the saints.
en.B: Dear friends, I was doing all I could to write to you about the salvation we hold in common, but I found I had to write and urge you to fight hard for the faith that was handed over to God's holy people once for all.
en.R: Dear friends, I was working hard to write to you about the salvation that all of us share. But I have had to write to you about something else. I am urging you to stand up and fight for the faith. This faith was handed over to God's holy people once, for all time.

es.L: Amados, poniendo todo empeño en escribir{{plural_you:les|os}} acerca de nuestra común salvación, tuve necesidad de escribir{{plural_you:les|os}}, exhortándo{{plural_you:los|os}} a luchar por la fe que fue entregada una vez para siempre a los santos.
es.B: Queridos, yo estaba haciendo todo lo posible por escribir{{plural_you:les|os}} acerca de la salvación que tenemos en común, pero me he visto obligado a escribir{{plural_you:les|os}} para rogar{{plural_you:les|os}} que {{plural_you:luchen|luchéis}} con empeño por la fe que fue entregada una vez para siempre al pueblo santo de Dios.
es.R: Queridos amigos, yo me estaba esforzando por escribir{{plural_you:les|os}} acerca de la salvación que todos compartimos. Pero he tenido que escribir{{plural_you:les|os}} sobre otra cosa. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} ruego que {{plural_you:defiendan|defendáis}} la fe y {{plural_you:luchen|luchéis}} por ella. Esta fe fue entregada al pueblo santo de Dios una sola vez, y es para siempre.

sw.L: Wapendwa, nikifanya bidii yote kuwaandikia kuhusu wokovu wetu wa pamoja, niliona ni lazima kuwaandikia, nikiwasihi mshindanie imani iliyokabidhiwa watakatifu mara moja kwa daima.
sw.B: Wapendwa, nilipokuwa nikifanya kila juhudi kuwaandikia kuhusu wokovu tunaoushiriki sote, niliona sina budi kuwaandikia na kuwasihi mpigane kwa bidii kwa ajili ya imani ambayo watu wa Mungu walio watakatifu walikabidhiwa mara moja kwa daima.
sw.R: Wapendwa wangu, nilikuwa nikijitahidi sana kuwaandikia kuhusu wokovu ambao sisi sote tunashiriki. Lakini imenibidi kuwaandikia kuhusu jambo jingine. Ninawasihi msimame na kuipigania imani. Watu wa Mungu walikabidhiwa imani hii mara moja tu, iwe yao kwa wakati wote.

fr.L: Bien-aimés, alors que je mettais tout mon zèle à vous écrire au sujet de notre salut commun, je me suis vu obligé de vous écrire pour vous exhorter à combattre pour la foi transmise une fois pour toutes aux saints.
fr.B: Mes chers amis, je faisais tout mon possible pour vous écrire au sujet du salut que nous avons en commun, mais je me suis vu obligé de vous écrire pour vous exhorter à lutter avec ardeur pour la foi qui a été transmise une fois pour toutes au peuple saint de Dieu.
fr.R: Mes chers amis, je travaillais dur pour vous écrire au sujet du salut que nous partageons tous. Mais j’ai dû vous écrire sur un autre sujet. Je vous encourage à vous lever et à vous battre pour la foi. Cette foi a été transmise au peuple saint de Dieu une seule fois, pour toujours.

ko.L: 사랑하는 여러분, 내가 우리가 함께 받은 구원에 대하여 여러분에게 쓰려고 온 힘을 다하던 중에, 성도들에게 단번에 맡겨진 믿음을 위하여 힘써 싸우라고 권하는 편지를 여러분에게 써야 할 필요를 느꼈습니다.
ko.B: 사랑하는 여러분, 나는 우리가 함께 누리는 구원에 대해 여러분에게 쓰려고 온 힘을 쏟고 있었습니다. 그런데 성도에게 단번에 영원히 맡겨진 믿음을 위해 힘써 싸우라고 여러분에게 권하는 편지를 써야 하겠다는 생각이 들었습니다.
ko.R: 사랑하는 여러분, 나는 우리 모두가 함께 받은 구원에 대해 여러분에게 편지를 쓰려고 열심히 준비하고 있었습니다. 그러나 다른 일에 대해 써야 하게 되었습니다. 나는 여러분에게 일어나서 믿음을 위해 싸우라고 권합니다. 이 믿음은 하나님의 거룩한 백성에게 단 한 번, 영원히 맡겨진 것입니다.

vi.L: Hỡi những người yêu dấu, trong khi tôi hết sức chuyên cần viết cho anh chị em về sự cứu rỗi chung của chúng ta, tôi thấy cần phải viết cho anh chị em, khuyên [anh chị em] chiến đấu cho đức tin đã được truyền lại một lần đủ cả cho các thánh đồ.
vi.B: Thưa anh chị em yêu dấu, tôi đang cố gắng hết sức để viết cho anh chị em về sự cứu rỗi mà chúng ta cùng có chung, nhưng tôi thấy mình phải viết để khuyên anh chị em hãy chiến đấu hết sức cho đức tin đã được truyền lại cho dân thánh của Đức Chúa Trời một lần đủ cả.
vi.R: Anh chị em thân mến, tôi đang cố gắng viết cho anh chị em về sự cứu rỗi mà tất cả chúng ta cùng có. Nhưng tôi phải viết cho anh chị em về một việc khác. Tôi khuyên anh chị em hãy đứng lên chiến đấu cho đức tin. Đức tin này đã được truyền lại cho dân thánh của Đức Chúa Trời một lần, cho mọi thời đại.

pt.L: Amados, empenhando-me ao máximo para lhes escrever sobre a nossa salvação comum, senti necessidade de lhes escrever, exortando [vocês] a lutar pela fé entregue de uma vez por todas aos santos.
pt.B: Queridos amigos, eu estava fazendo todo o possível para escrever a vocês sobre a salvação que temos em comum, mas vi que precisava escrever para exortá-los a lutar com empenho pela fé que foi entregue de uma vez por todas ao povo santo de Deus.
pt.R: Queridos amigos, eu estava me esforçando muito para escrever a vocês sobre a salvação que todos nós compartilhamos. Mas tive de escrever a vocês sobre outra coisa. Peço que vocês se levantem e lutem pela fé. Essa fé foi entregue ao povo santo de Deus uma vez, para sempre.

am.L: የተወደዳችሁ ሆይ፣ ስለ ጋራ መዳናችን ልጽፍላችሁ ትጋትን ሁሉ ሳደርግ፣ ለቅዱሳን አንድ ጊዜ ፈጽሞ ስለ ተሰጠው እምነት እንድትጋደሉ እየመከርኳችሁ ልጽፍላችሁ ግድ ሆነብኝ።
am.B: ወዳጆቼ ሆይ፣ ሁላችንም ስለምንካፈለው መዳን ልጽፍላችሁ በብርቱ እየጣርኩ ሳለሁ፣ ለእግዚአብሔር ቅዱሳን ሕዝብ አንድ ጊዜ ለሁልጊዜ ስለ ተሰጠው እምነት አጥብቃችሁ እንድትጋደሉ ልመክራችሁና ልጽፍላችሁ ግድ ሆነብኝ።
am.R: ውድ ወዳጆቼ፣ ሁላችንም ስለምንካፈለው መዳን ልጽፍላችሁ በብርቱ እየሠራሁ ነበር። ነገር ግን ስለ ሌላ ነገር ልጽፍላችሁ ግድ ሆነብኝ። ተነሡና ስለ እምነቱ ታገሉ ብዬ እመክራችኋለሁ። ይህ እምነት ለእግዚአብሔር ቅዱሳን ሕዝብ አንድ ጊዜ ለዘለቄታው ተሰጥቷል።

decisions.choice: beloved: people Jude loves, and whom God loves
decisions.reason: Ἀγαπητοί is used in letters for dear fellow believers (1 John 2:7; 2 Peter 3:1). It echoes verse 1, where the readers are loved by God. Jude uses it three times (verses 3, 17, 20), each time to turn from the false teachers to his readers.

decisions.choice: two kinds of writing: the letter he was eager to write about salvation, and the urgent appeal he found he had to write instead
alternatives: one letter: he was eager to write, and felt it necessary to do so as an appeal
decisions.reason: The present infinitive γράφειν, "to write", and the aorist γράψαι, "to write", stand side by side: he was busy with one kind of letter when a pressing need made him write this one. Verse 4 gives the need: false teachers have slipped in.

decisions.choice: our common salvation: the salvation all believers share, Jude and his readers alike
decisions.reason: κοινῆς means shared or held in common (Titus 1:4 speaks of "a common faith"). The salvation Jude meant to write about belongs to all of them equally.

decisions.choice: contend: struggle hard on behalf of something, as an athlete strains in a contest
decisions.reason: ἐπαγωνίζομαι is found only here in the New Testament. It is built on the word for a contest or a struggle, with a prefix that points to what the struggle is for. The readers are to strive for the faith; verses 20-23 show that this means building themselves up, praying and rescuing others, not only arguing.

decisions.choice: the faith handed over once for all to the saints: the truth that is believed, given to God's people once and complete
decisions.reason: Here πίστει is the faith that is believed, the content of the message, rather than the act of trusting (compare verse 20, "your most holy faith"). παραδοθείσῃ is the verb for handing on a teaching or tradition (1 Corinthians 11:2; 15:3; 2 Peter 2:21). ἅπαξ, "once for all", means it was given once and needs nothing added; the same word is in verse 5. The saints, or holy ones, are God's people.

decisions.choice: Dear friends
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "beloved"; Balanced and Readable say "dear friends", as in 1 John and 2 Peter, since "beloved" is no longer an ordinary way to address people.

decisions.choice: contend for (L); fight hard for (B); stand up and fight for (R)
decisions.reason: The word speaks of a hard struggle (m4). "Contend" keeps the sense at Literal; Balanced and Readable use plainer words for the same effort.

decisions.choice: the saints (L); God's holy people (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Saints" now suggests especially holy individuals. Balanced and Readable say what the word means here: all of God's people, as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: I have had to write to you about something else
alternatives: I had to write to you
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit the change of subject that the two infinitives imply (m2).

decisions.choice: amados (L); queridos (B); queridos amigos (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 3:1: Literal keeps "amados" (loved ones); Balanced uses "queridos", the ordinary way to address people one loves; Readable says "queridos amigos" as the English does. The same in verses 17 and 20.

decisions.choice: wapendwa (L, B); wapendwa wangu (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 3:1: "wapendwa" (those who are loved) says what the Greek word says; "wapenzi" today often means sweethearts. Readable adds "wangu" (my) for warmth. The same in verses 17 and 20.

decisions.choice: Bien-aimés (L); Mes chers amis (B, R); aux saints (L), au peuple saint de Dieu (B, R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Bien-aimés" is no longer an ordinary way to address people; Balanced and Readable say "mes chers amis", as the English does (m1). "Les saints" now suggests exceptional individuals, so Balanced and Readable say who they are, as in Colossians and Ephesians.

decisions.choice: "사랑하는 여러분" for beloved (for the whole letter); "성도" (L, B), "하나님의 거룩한 백성" (R) for the saints; "믿음" for the faith
decisions.reason: As in the Korean of the other letters. The saints are God's people (as settled for "성도" in the Korean Colossians and Romans), and "the faith" here is the truth that is believed (meaning decision), still "믿음", as the key term at every level.

decisions.choice: "힘써 싸우다" for contend; "단번에" (L), "단번에 영원히" (B), "단 한 번, 영원히" (R) for once for all
decisions.reason: To contend is to struggle hard on behalf of something, as an athlete strains in a contest (meaning decision); Korean "힘써 싸우다" keeps the effort. "Once for all" means given once and complete (meaning decision), which Balanced and Readable spell out.

decisions.choice: "các thánh đồ" (L); "dân thánh của Đức Chúa Trời" (B, R) for the saints; "đức tin" for the faith
decisions.reason: The forms of the Vietnamese Colossians (1:4) and Romans, so that the whole church is plainly meant. The faith here is the truth that is believed (m5), still "đức tin", the key term. "Hỡi những người yêu dấu", "Thưa anh chị em yêu dấu", "Anh chị em thân mến" for beloved follow 1 Peter 2:11.

decisions.choice: "chiến đấu cho" (L), "chiến đấu hết sức cho" (B), "đứng lên chiến đấu cho" (R) for contend
decisions.reason: To contend is to struggle hard on behalf of something, as an athlete strains in a contest (m4); "chiến đấu" keeps the effort, where "bênh vực" would be only to defend in words.

decisions.choice: Amados (L); Queridos amigos (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole letter (also verses 17 and 20), as in 2 Peter 3:1.

decisions.choice: የተወደዳችሁ ሆይ (beloved, L), ወዳጆቼ ሆይ (B), ውድ ወዳጆቼ (R), as in 1 John; እንድትጋደሉ (that you contend, L, B), ታገሉ (fight, R); ቅዱሳን (the saints, L), የእግዚአብሔር ቅዱሳን ሕዝብ (God's holy people, B, R)
decisions.reason: The address follows the Amharic of 1 John and Paul's letters. "መጋደል" is to struggle hard, as an athlete strains in a contest (meaning decision m4), and it is a struggle for the faith, not an argument. The saints are God's people (m5), as the English Balanced and Readable say.

source.text: παρεισέδυσαν γάρ τινες ἄνθρωποι, οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο τὸ κρίμα, ἀσεβεῖς, τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριτα μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειαν καὶ τὸν μόνον δεσπότην καὶ κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἀρνούμενοι.

records.literal_gloss: Slipped in for certain people, the [ones] long ago having been written beforehand for this the judgment, ungodly [ones], the of the God of us grace changing into sensuality and the only Master and Lord of us Jesus Christ denying.

en.L: For certain {{gender:people|men}} have slipped in, who long ago were written about beforehand for this judgment, ungodly [people], changing our God's grace into sensuality and denying our only Master and Lord, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: For some {{gender:people|men}} have slipped in among you without being noticed. Long ago it was written that they would face this judgment. They are ungodly people who twist our God's grace into an excuse for shameless living, and who disown Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, our only Master and Lord.
en.R: I say this because some {{gender:people|men}} have sneaked in among you without anyone noticing. Long ago it was written that people like them would be judged. They do not honor God. They take our God's grace and use it as an excuse to live shamelessly. And they turn against Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who alone is our Master and Lord.

es.L: Porque se han infiltrado {{gender:ciertas personas|ciertos hombres}}, de quienes desde hace mucho se escribió de antemano para este juicio, gente impía, que convierte la gracia de nuestro Dios en desenfreno y niega a nuestro único Amo y Señor, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Porque {{gender:algunas personas|algunos hombres}} se han infiltrado entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sin que nadie lo notara. Hace mucho tiempo quedó escrito que les esperaba este juicio. Son gente impía que hace de la gracia de nuestro Dios una excusa para el desenfreno, y que reniega de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, nuestro único Amo y Señor.
es.R: Digo esto porque {{gender:algunas personas|algunos hombres}} se han metido entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a escondidas, sin que nadie se diera cuenta. Hace mucho tiempo quedó escrito que la gente como ellos sería juzgada. No honran a Dios. Toman la gracia de nuestro Dios y la usan como excusa para llevar una vida desvergonzada. Y se vuelven contra {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, el único que es nuestro Amo y Señor.

sw.L: Kwa maana watu fulani wamejipenyeza kwa siri, ambao tangu zamani waliandikwa mapema kwa ajili ya hukumu hii, [watu] wasiomcha Mungu, wakiigeuza neema ya Mungu wetu kuwa ukosefu wa haya, na wakimkana Bwana wetu wa pekee, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kwa maana watu fulani wamejipenyeza kati yenu bila kutambuliwa. Zamani iliandikwa kwamba wangeipata hukumu hii. Ni watu wasiomcha Mungu, wanaoigeuza neema ya Mungu wetu kuwa kisingizio cha maisha yasiyo na haya, na wanaomkana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Bwana wetu wa pekee.
sw.R: Nasema hivi kwa sababu watu fulani wameingia kati yenu kwa siri, bila mtu yeyote kutambua. Zamani iliandikwa kwamba watu kama hao watahukumiwa. Hawamheshimu Mungu. Wanaichukua neema ya Mungu wetu na kuitumia kama kisingizio cha kuishi bila haya. Tena wanamgeuka Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ambaye peke yake ndiye Bwana wetu.

fr.L: Car certains {{gender:individus|hommes}} se sont glissés [parmi vous], eux qui depuis longtemps ont été inscrits d’avance pour ce jugement, des impies, qui changent la grâce de notre Dieu en débauche et renient notre seul Maître et Seigneur, Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Car certains {{gender:individus|hommes}} se sont glissés parmi vous sans qu’on les remarque. Il y a longtemps qu’il a été écrit qu’ils subiraient ce jugement. Ce sont des impies, qui font de la grâce de notre Dieu un prétexte à la débauche, et qui renient Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, notre seul Maître et Seigneur.
fr.R: Je vous dis cela parce que certains {{gender:individus|hommes}} se sont introduits parmi vous sans que personne le remarque. Il y a longtemps, il a été écrit que des gens comme eux seraient jugés. Ils ne respectent pas Dieu. Ils prennent la grâce de notre Dieu et s’en servent comme excuse pour vivre sans aucune pudeur. Et ils se tournent contre Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, qui est notre seul Maître et Seigneur.

ko.L: 어떤 사람들이 몰래 들어왔기 때문입니다. 그들은 오래전에 이 심판을 받도록 미리 기록된 사람들이며, 경건하지 않은 사람들로서, 우리 하나님의 은혜를 방탕으로 바꾸고, 우리의 유일한 주인이시며 주님이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 부인합니다.
ko.B: 어떤 사람들이 여러분 가운데 아무도 모르게 몰래 들어왔기 때문입니다. 그들이 이런 심판을 받으리라는 것은 오래전에 기록되었습니다. 그들은 경건하지 않은 사람들로서, 우리 하나님의 은혜를 방탕한 생활의 핑계로 바꾸고, 우리의 유일한 주인이시며 주님이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 부인합니다.
ko.R: 내가 이렇게 말하는 것은, 어떤 사람들이 아무도 모르게 여러분 가운데 몰래 들어왔기 때문입니다. 오래전에 그런 사람들이 심판을 받으리라고 기록되었습니다. 그들은 하나님을 공경하지 않습니다. 그들은 우리 하나님의 은혜를 부끄러운 줄 모르고 사는 핑계로 삼습니다. 그리고 우리의 오직 한 분 주인이시며 주님이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 배반합니다.

vi.L: Vì có mấy người đã lẻn vào, là những người từ lâu đã được chép trước cho sự phán xét này, là những kẻ không tin kính, biến ân điển của Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta thành sự phóng đãng và chối bỏ Đấng Chủ Tể và Chúa duy nhất của chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Vì có mấy người đã lén lút lọt vào giữa anh chị em mà không ai hay biết. Từ lâu đã có lời chép rằng họ sẽ phải chịu sự phán xét này. Họ là những kẻ không tin kính, bóp méo ân điển của Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta thành cớ để sống trơ trẽn, và chối bỏ Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, là Chủ Tể và Chúa duy nhất của chúng ta.
vi.R: Tôi nói điều này vì có mấy người đã lẻn vào giữa anh chị em mà không ai để ý. Từ lâu đã có lời chép rằng những người như họ sẽ bị phán xét. Họ không tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời. pt.L: Pois se infiltraram certos {{gender:indivíduos|homens}}, que há muito tempo foram inscritos de antemão para este julgamento, ímpios, que transformam a graça do nosso Deus em libertinagem e negam o nosso único Soberano e Senhor, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.B: Pois alguns {{gender:indivíduos|homens}} se infiltraram no meio de vocês sem serem notados. Há muito tempo foi escrito que eles enfrentariam este julgamento. São ímpios, que distorcem a graça do nosso Deus, fazendo dela uma desculpa para uma vida desavergonhada, e que renegam Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, o nosso único Soberano e Senhor.
pt.R: Digo isso porque alguns {{gender:indivíduos|homens}} entraram às escondidas no meio de vocês, sem que ninguém percebesse. Há muito tempo foi escrito que pessoas como eles seriam julgadas. Eles não honram a Deus. Pegam a graça do nosso Deus e a usam como desculpa para viver sem nenhuma vergonha. E se voltam contra Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, o único que é o nosso Dono e Senhor.

am.L: አንዳንድ ሰዎች ሾልከው ገብተዋልና፤ እነርሱም ከብዙ ጊዜ በፊት ለዚህ ፍርድ አስቀድመው የተጻፈባቸው፣ እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩ፣ የአምላካችንን ጸጋ ወደ ሴሰኝነት የሚለውጡ፣ ብቸኛ ገዥያችንንና ጌታችንን ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስን|መሲሕን}} የሚክዱ ናቸው።
am.B: አንዳንድ ሰዎች ሳይታወቁ ሾልከው በመካከላችሁ ገብተዋልና። ይህ ፍርድ እንደሚደርስባቸው ከብዙ ጊዜ በፊት ተጽፏል። እነርሱ እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩ ናቸው፤ የአምላካችንን ጸጋ ለሴሰኝነት ምክንያት ያደርጋሉ፤ ብቸኛ ገዥያችንና ጌታችን የሆነውን ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስን|መሲሕን}} ይክዳሉ።
am.R: ይህን የምላችሁ አንዳንድ ሰዎች ማንም ሳያስተውላቸው ሾልከው በመካከላችሁ ስለ ገቡ ነው። እንደ እነርሱ ያሉ ሰዎች እንደሚፈረድባቸው ከብዙ ጊዜ በፊት ተጽፏል። እግዚአብሔርን አያከብሩም። የአምላካችንን ጸጋ ወስደው ያለ ኀፍረት ለመኖር ምክንያት ያደርጉታል። ብቻውን ገዥያችንና ጌታችን የሆነውን ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስን|መሲሕን}} ይክዱታል።

decisions.choice: slipped in: came in secretly, unnoticed
decisions.reason: παρεισδύω means to slip in alongside, without being noticed. Galatians 2:4 uses a similar picture, and 2 Peter 2:1 a related verb. γάρ, "for", gives the reason for the appeal in verse 3. These people are inside the church and share its meals (verse 12).

decisions.choice: long ago written about beforehand for this judgment: the judgment on such people was set down in writing long before they came
alternatives: long ago appointed (or designated) for this condemnation
decisions.reason: προγράφω means to write beforehand (Romans 15:4) or to post a public notice (Galatians 3:1). With πάλαι, "long ago", the first sense is most likely. Jude goes on to show where it was written: the examples from Israel's Scriptures (verses 5-7 and 11), the prophecy of Enoch (verses 14-15) and the apostles' warning (verses 17-18). "This judgment" points ahead to those passages. The text speaks of the judgment that awaits them; it does not say how they came to be what they are.

decisions.choice: ungodly: people who live without reverence for God
decisions.reason: ἀσεβής and its related words come six times in Jude, four of them in the prophecy of verse 15 and once more in verse 18. They describe people who treat God without reverence, and it shows in what they do.

decisions.choice: changing God's grace into sensuality: treating God's free kindness as permission for unrestrained living
decisions.reason: μετατίθημι means to change something or move it to another use. ἀσέλγεια is open, unrestrained indulgence, especially sexual, that does not care who sees it (as in 2 Peter 2:2, 7, 18). They take God's grace, his undeserved favor that forgives, and make it a reason to sin freely, the error Paul answers in Romans 6:1-2.

decisions.choice: our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ: one person, Jesus Christ, called both Master and Lord
alternatives: two persons: the only Master (God), and our Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: One article, τὸν, governs both nouns, δεσπότην and κύριον, and "our" and the name Jesus Christ follow them, so the natural reading is one person with two titles, as in 2 Peter 1:1, "our God and Savior Jesus Christ". δεσπότης is the word for a slave's owner. It is used of God (Luke 2:29; Acts 4:24; Revelation 6:10) and of Christ in 2 Peter 2:1, "the Master who bought them", the parallel to this verse. "Only" recalls the confession that the LORD alone is God (Deuteronomy 6:4); here it is said of Jesus Christ.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the only Master"
alternatives: "the only Master, God, and our Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "God" after "Master", and the King James Version follows them ("the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ"). With that word the verse reads more easily as naming two persons. The earlier manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: denying: disowning him, above all by how they live
decisions.reason: ἀρνέομαι means to say no to someone, to disown them. Nothing in Jude says that they denied Christ in words; their unrestrained, ungodly life rejects his rule (compare Titus 1:16). Verse 8 says the same in other words: they reject lordship.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωποι means human beings, and the text does not say whether women were among them. "People" is the default; "men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: sensuality (L); an excuse for shameless living (B); an excuse to live shamelessly (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2, Literal says "sensuality" and Balanced and Readable describe the behavior as shameless (m4). "An excuse for" says in plain words what turning grace into sensuality means.

decisions.choice: disown (B); turn against (R)
decisions.reason: "Deny" in current English usually means to say something is not true. Balanced and Readable use words for rejecting a person, as in 2 Peter 2:1 (m7).

decisions.choice: They do not honor God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "ungodly" means, as in 2 Peter 2 (m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:ciertas personas|ciertos hombres}} (L); {{gender:algunas personas|algunos hombres}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωποι means human beings, and the text does not say whether women were among them. The span covers the article as well as the noun, since Spanish articles agree. Literal goes on with "gente impía", which agrees with neither noun, so no other word has to change with the setting.

decisions.choice: nuestro único Amo y Señor
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:1, "Amo" is the owner of slaves, the sense of the Greek word (m5), and "Señor" stays the word for Lord. Spanish can keep the two titles apart, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: desenfreno (L, B); una vida desvergonzada (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as in 2 Peter 2:2, 7 and 18: open, unrestrained living that does not care who sees it (m4). "Lascivia" would narrow it to sexual sin. Readable says "desvergonzada" (shameless), as the Readable of 2 Peter 2 does.

decisions.choice: Bwana wetu wa pekee
alternatives: Mtawala wetu wa pekee na Bwana wetu
Bwana na Mmiliki wetu wa pekee
decisions.reason: Swahili "Bwana" is both a slave's master, the sense of δεσπότην (m5), and the word for Lord, κύριον, so one word carries both titles, as in 2 Peter 2:1 ("Bwana aliyewanunua"). Saying "Bwana ... na Bwana" would sound like two persons, the opposite of what the grammar shows. "Mtawala" (ruler) would keep two words but lose the picture of a slave's owner. A reviewer should judge whether the loss of the second title is acceptable.

decisions.choice: ukosefu wa haya (L); maisha yasiyo na haya (B); kuishi bila haya (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:2, 7 and 18 and Galatians 5:19. "Ufisadi" today most often means corruption in public office, and "uasherati" would narrow the word to sexual sin.

decisions.choice: watu, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Watu" already means people, men and women; "wanaume" means males and would change the meaning, so Swahili has no counterpart to the English gender span.

decisions.choice: certains {{gender:individus|hommes}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, and the text does not say whether women were among them. "Individus" is inclusive, keeps the slightly distant tone of the Greek "certain people", and is masculine like "hommes", so the words that agree with it ("glissés") are the same under both options.

decisions.choice: renient (L, B); se tournent contre (R)
decisions.reason: French "renier" means to disown a person one belonged to, which is the sense here (m7), so it needs none of the care that English "deny" does.

decisions.choice: "어떤 사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The word means human beings; Korean "사람" includes men and women and has no generic masculine, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "은혜" (key term) at every level; "방탕" (L), as in 2 Peter 2:2; "유일한 주인이시며 주님이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "our only Master and Lord" as one person, Jesus Christ, called both, and footnotes it; Korean "-이시며 ... -이신" joins both titles to the one name, as in 2 Peter 1:1. "주인" for Master, as in 2 Peter 2:1, keeps the picture of the owner.

decisions.choice: "mấy người" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" is a person of either sex, so the gender setting has no second wording to offer.

decisions.choice: "Chủ Tể và Chúa" for Master and Lord, as in 2 Peter 2:1
decisions.reason: One person, Jesus Christ, is called both Master and Lord (m5). "Chủ Tể" is the word the Vietnamese 2 Peter uses for the same Greek word, kept apart from "Chúa".

decisions.choice: {{gender:indivíduos|homens}}
decisions.reason: The English default is "people". Portuguese "pessoas" is feminine, and every word that follows would have to change with the setting ("ímpias", "inscritas"); "indivíduos" means persons of either sex but is grammatically masculine, so only the noun changes. Its slightly cold tone suits Jude's description.

decisions.choice: libertinagem (L); vida desavergonhada (B, R); o Soberano (L, B), o Dono (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:1-2, the parallel passage: the same words for the shameless conduct (m4) and for the owner's title (m5).

decisions.choice: እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩ (the ungodly, L, B), እግዚአብሔርን አያከብሩም (they do not honour God, R), through the letter; ሴሰኝነት (sensuality); ገዥ (Master) beside ጌታ (Lord)
decisions.reason: "Ungodly" is the key word of Jude (verses 4, 15, 18), and Amharic keeps the term of the Amharic 2 Peter 2:5-6, "እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩ", with Readable's "do not honour God", so the repetitions can be heard (meaning decision m3). "ገዥ" is the one who rules, kept apart from "ጌታ" because the Greek has two titles for one person, Jesus Christ (m5).

decisions.choice: ሰዎች (people), with no gender span
decisions.reason: "ሰዎች" already means people, men and women, and Amharic has no second wording meaning "men" in the old generic sense, so the setting has nothing to switch; the same holds for ሰው, ማንም and the generic masculine verb through the letter.

source.text: Ὑπομνῆσαι δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι, εἰδότας ὑμᾶς ἅπαξ πάντα, ὅτι Ἰησοῦς λαὸν ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου σώσας τὸ δεύτερον τοὺς μὴ πιστεύσαντας ἀπώλεσεν, ἀγγέλους τε τοὺς μὴ τηρήσαντας τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχὴν ἀλλὰ ἀπολιπόντας τὸ ἴδιον οἰκητήριον εἰς κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τετήρηκεν·

en.L: But I want to remind you, though you know all things once for all, that Jesus, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, the second time destroyed the ones who did not believe; \v 6 and angels who did not keep their own position but deserted their own dwelling {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept for [the] judgment of [the] great day in everlasting bonds under gloom.
en.B: Now I want to remind you of something, though you know it all already. Jesus saved a people out of the land of Egypt, but afterward {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed those among them who did not believe. \v 6 And the angels who did not stay in the place of authority that was theirs, but abandoned their own dwelling, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept in everlasting chains in deepest darkness, ready for judgment when the great day comes.
en.R: You already know all this, but I want to remind you of it. Jesus saved the people of Israel and brought them out of the land of Egypt. But later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed the ones who did not believe. \v 6 Remember the angels who did not stay in the place of authority God had given them. They left the home where they belonged. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept them in the dark, in chains that will last forever. They are being held there until the great day of judgment.

es.L: Pero quiero recordar{{plural_you:les|os}}, aunque {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} todo una vez para siempre, que Jesús, habiendo salvado a un pueblo de la tierra de Egipto, la segunda vez destruyó a los que no creyeron; \v 6 y a [los] ángeles que no guardaron su propia posición, sino que abandonaron su propia morada, los ha guardado para [el] juicio del gran día en cadenas perpetuas bajo oscuridad.
es.B: Ahora quiero recordar{{plural_you:les|os}} algo, aunque ya lo {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} todo. Jesús salvó a un pueblo sacándolo de la tierra de Egipto, pero después destruyó a los de ese pueblo que no creyeron. \v 6 Y a los ángeles que no se mantuvieron en el lugar de autoridad que les correspondía, sino que abandonaron su propia morada, los ha guardado en cadenas perpetuas, en profunda oscuridad, para el juicio del gran día.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} ya {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} todo esto, pero quiero {{plural_you:recordárselo|recordároslo}}. Jesús salvó al pueblo de Israel y lo sacó de la tierra de Egipto. Pero más tarde destruyó a los que no creyeron. \v 6 {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} también a los ángeles que no se quedaron en el lugar de autoridad que Dios les había dado. Dejaron el hogar al que pertenecían. Por eso {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los tiene guardados en la oscuridad, con cadenas que durarán para siempre. Allí están presos hasta el gran día del juicio.

sw.L: Lakini nataka kuwakumbusha, ingawa mnajua mambo yote mara moja kwa daima, kwamba Yesu, akiisha kuwaokoa watu kutoka nchi ya Misri, mara ya pili aliwaangamiza wale ambao hawakuamini; \v 6 na malaika ambao hawakulinda nafasi yao wenyewe, bali waliacha makao yao wenyewe, amewalinda kwa ajili ya hukumu ya siku ile kuu katika vifungo vya daima chini ya giza.
sw.B: Sasa nataka kuwakumbusha jambo fulani, ingawa tayari mnayajua yote. Yesu aliwaokoa watu kutoka nchi ya Misri, lakini baadaye aliwaangamiza wale miongoni mwao ambao hawakuamini. \v 6 Na malaika ambao hawakukaa katika nafasi ya mamlaka waliyopewa, bali waliyaacha makao yao wenyewe, amewalinda katika minyororo ya daima, katika giza nene, tayari kwa hukumu ya siku ile kuu.
sw.R: Mnajua tayari mambo haya yote, lakini nataka kuwakumbusha. Yesu aliwaokoa watu wa Israeli na kuwatoa katika nchi ya Misri. Lakini baadaye aliwaangamiza wale ambao hawakuamini. \v 6 Kumbukeni pia malaika ambao hawakukaa katika nafasi ya mamlaka ambayo Mungu aliwapa. Waliyaacha makao yaliyokuwa yao. Kwa hiyo amewafunga gizani kwa minyororo itakayodumu milele. Wanalindwa huko mpaka siku ile kuu ya hukumu.

fr.L: Or je veux vous rappeler, bien que vous sachiez tout une fois pour toutes, que Jésus, ayant sauvé un peuple du pays d’Égypte, a fait périr la seconde fois ceux qui n’avaient pas cru ; \v 6 et les anges qui n’ont pas gardé leur rang, mais ont abandonné leur propre demeure, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a gardés pour le jugement du grand jour dans des liens perpétuels, sous l’obscurité.
fr.B: Je veux maintenant vous rappeler une chose, bien que vous la sachiez déjà. Jésus a sauvé un peuple en le faisant sortir du pays d’Égypte, mais ensuite {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait périr ceux d’entre eux qui n’avaient pas cru. \v 6 Quant aux anges qui ne sont pas restés dans la position d’autorité qui était la leur, mais qui ont abandonné leur propre demeure, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a gardés dans des chaînes perpétuelles, au plus profond des ténèbres, pour le jugement du grand jour.
fr.R: Vous savez déjà tout cela, mais je veux vous le rappeler. Jésus a sauvé le peuple d’Israël et l’a fait sortir du pays d’Égypte. Mais plus tard, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait mourir ceux qui n’avaient pas cru. \v 6 Souvenez-vous des anges qui ne sont pas restés à la place d’autorité que Dieu leur avait donnée. Ils ont quitté le lieu où ils devaient vivre. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a gardés dans l’obscurité, attachés avec des chaînes qui dureront toujours. Ils sont retenus là jusqu’au grand jour du jugement.

ko.L: 여러분이 모든 것을 단번에 알고 있지만, 나는 여러분에게 일깨워 주고 싶습니다. 예수께서 한 백성을 이집트 땅에서 구원하시고, 그다음에 믿지 않은 사람들을 멸하셨습니다. \v 6 또 자기들의 지위를 지키지 않고 자기들의 거처를 떠난 천사들을, 그분은 큰 날의 심판 때까지 영원한 사슬로 묶어 어둠 아래 지키셨습니다.
ko.B: 여러분은 이미 모든 것을 알고 있지만, 나는 여러분에게 한 가지를 일깨워 주고 싶습니다. 예수께서 한 백성을 이집트 땅에서 구원하셨지만, 나중에 그들 가운데 믿지 않은 사람들을 멸하셨습니다. \v 6 또 자기들에게 주어진 권위의 자리를 지키지 않고 자기들의 거처를 버린 천사들을, 그분은 큰 날의 심판 때까지 영원한 사슬로 묶어 깊은 어둠 속에 가두어 지키셨습니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 이미 이 모든 것을 알고 있지만, 다시 일깨워 주고 싶습니다. 예수께서 이스라엘 백성을 구원하셔서 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 내셨습니다. 그러나 나중에 믿지 않은 사람들을 멸하셨습니다. \v 6 하나님께서 주신 권위의 자리를 지키지 않은 천사들을 기억하십시오. 그들은 자기들이 있어야 할 거처를 떠났습니다. 그래서 그분은 그들을 어둠 속에서 영원히 풀리지 않을 사슬로 묶어 두셨습니다. 그들은 심판의 큰 날까지 그곳에 갇혀 있습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng tôi muốn nhắc lại cho anh chị em, dù anh chị em đã biết mọi điều một lần đủ cả, rằng Đức Giê-xu, sau khi đã cứu một dân ra khỏi đất Ai Cập, lần thứ hai đã hủy diệt những người không tin; \v 6 và các thiên sứ không giữ địa vị của mình mà bỏ chỗ ở riêng của mình, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã giam giữ trong xiềng xích đời đời dưới sự tối tăm cho đến sự phán xét của ngày lớn.
vi.B: Bây giờ tôi muốn nhắc anh chị em một điều, dù anh chị em đã biết tất cả rồi. Đức Giê-xu đã cứu một dân ra khỏi đất Ai Cập, nhưng sau đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hủy diệt những người trong họ không tin. \v 6 Còn các thiên sứ không ở trong địa vị quyền hành đã được giao cho mình mà bỏ chỗ ở riêng của mình, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã giam giữ họ trong xiềng xích đời đời, trong bóng tối dày đặc, để chờ sự phán xét khi ngày lớn đến.
vi.R: Anh chị em đã biết tất cả những điều này rồi, nhưng tôi muốn nhắc lại cho anh chị em. Đức Giê-xu đã cứu dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và đem họ ra khỏi đất Ai Cập. Nhưng về sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hủy diệt những người không tin. \v 6 Hãy nhớ đến các thiên sứ không chịu ở trong địa vị quyền hành Đức Chúa Trời đã giao cho họ. Họ đã bỏ nơi ở mà mình thuộc về. Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã giam họ trong bóng tối, trong những xiềng xích còn mãi mãi. Họ đang bị giam giữ ở đó cho đến ngày phán xét lớn.

pt.L: Mas quero lembrá-los, embora vocês saibam todas as coisas de uma vez por todas, que Jesus, tendo salvado um povo da terra do Egito, na segunda vez destruiu os que não creram; \v 6 e anjos que não guardaram a sua própria posição, mas abandonaram a sua própria morada, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tem guardado para [o] julgamento do grande dia em cadeias perpétuas, sob [a] escuridão.
pt.B: Agora quero lembrar vocês de uma coisa, embora vocês já saibam tudo isso. Jesus salvou um povo, tirando-o da terra do Egito, mas depois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} destruiu aqueles que, entre eles, não creram. \v 6 E os anjos que não permaneceram na posição de autoridade que era deles, mas abandonaram a sua própria morada, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os tem guardado em correntes perpétuas, na mais profunda escuridão, prontos para o julgamento quando chegar o grande dia.
pt.R: Vocês já sabem tudo isso, mas quero lembrá-los. Jesus salvou o povo de Israel e o tirou da terra do Egito. Mas depois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} destruiu os que não acreditaram. \v 6 Lembrem-se dos anjos que não ficaram no lugar de autoridade que Deus lhes tinha dado. Eles deixaram o lar a que pertenciam. Por isso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os tem guardado na escuridão, em correntes que vão durar para sempre. Eles estão presos ali até o grande dia do julgamento.

am.L: እናንተ ሁሉን አንድ ጊዜ ፈጽማችሁ የምታውቁ ብትሆኑም፣ ላሳስባችሁ እወዳለሁ፤ ኢየሱስ ሕዝብን ከግብፅ ምድር አድኖ፣ ሁለተኛ ጊዜ ያላመኑትን አጠፋ፤ \v 6 የራሳቸውንም ሥልጣን ያልጠበቁትን፣ ነገር ግን የገዛ መኖሪያቸውን የተዉትን መላእክት ለታላቁ ቀን ፍርድ በዘላለም እስራት ከጨለማ በታች ጠብቋቸዋል።
am.B: ይህን ሁሉ አስቀድማችሁ የምታውቁ ቢሆንም፣ አንድ ነገር ላስታውሳችሁ እወዳለሁ። ኢየሱስ ሕዝብን ከግብፅ ምድር አዳነ፤ በኋላ ግን ከእነርሱ መካከል ያላመኑትን አጠፋ። \v 6 የተሰጣቸውን የሥልጣን ስፍራ ያልጠበቁትንና የገዛ መኖሪያቸውን የተዉትን መላእክትም ታላቁ ቀን ሲመጣ ለሚሆነው ፍርድ በዘላለም ሰንሰለት በድቅድቅ ጨለማ ውስጥ ጠብቋቸዋል።
am.R: ይህን ሁሉ አስቀድማችሁ ታውቃላችሁ፤ ቢሆንም ላስታውሳችሁ እፈልጋለሁ። ኢየሱስ የእስራኤልን ሕዝብ አዳናቸው፤ ከግብፅ ምድርም አወጣቸው። በኋላ ግን ያላመኑትን አጠፋቸው። \v 6 እግዚአብሔር በሰጣቸው የሥልጣን ስፍራ ያልቆዩትን መላእክት አስታውሱ። የሚገባቸውን መኖሪያ ትተው ሄዱ። ስለዚህ ለዘላለም በማይፈታ ሰንሰለት በጨለማ ውስጥ ጠብቋቸዋል። እስከ ታላቁ የፍርድ ቀን ድረስ በዚያ ተይዘው ይቆያሉ።

decisions.choice: I want to remind you, though you know all things once for all: Jude tells them nothing new
decisions.reason: Ὑπομνῆσαι, "to remind", and εἰδότας, "knowing", say that what follows is what the readers have already been taught; Jude calls them to remember it, as 2 Peter 1:12-13 does. In the SBLGNT ἅπαξ, "once for all", goes with "knowing": they have been fully taught.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Jesus"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads Ἰησοῦς, "Jesus", as the one who saved the people out of Egypt. The manuscripts differ here more than anywhere else in Jude. "Jesus" is the reading of some important early manuscripts, among them Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus, and of some early translations. Others, among them Codex Sinaiticus and most later manuscripts, read "the Lord"; a few read "God"; and the early papyrus P72 has an unusual "God Christ". "Jesus" is the harder reading: it is easy to see why a copyist would change it to "the Lord" or "God", and hard to see why anyone would change those to "Jesus". That is the main reason for preferring it, but the evidence is divided, and "the Lord" is also well supported. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus as the one who saved Israel from Egypt: Jude speaks of Jesus as present and acting in Israel's history
alternatives: Joshua, whose name is the same in Greek
decisions.reason: If "Jesus" is the original reading (m2), Jude places Jesus Christ, his only Master and Lord (verse 4), in Israel's past: he saved the people out of Egypt, later judged them, and keeps the rebel angels for judgment (verse 6). Paul writes in a similar way when he says that the rock that followed Israel was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4). The reading does not mean that the name Jesus was known in Moses' day, and it does not deny that the LORD, Israel's God, brought them out; it says that the one Christians call Jesus was at work there. In Greek Ἰησοῦς is also the name Joshua, but Joshua did not bring the people out of Egypt, destroy the unbelievers or keep angels for judgment, so that reading is unlikely. With "the Lord" the verse would leave open whether God or Christ is meant.

decisions.choice: saved out of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe: the exodus, and the generation that died in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The people were brought out of Egypt (Exodus 12-14), but when they refused to trust God and enter the land, that generation died in the wilderness (Numbers 14:11, 26-35; compare 1 Corinthians 10:1-5; Hebrews 3:16-19). τὸ δεύτερον, "the second time", most likely means afterward, the second act after the saving: being rescued once did not protect those who later refused to believe.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "once for all" goes with "knowing"
alternatives: "once" goes with "saved": "having once saved a people ... the second time destroyed"
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT ἅπαξ stands before πάντα and goes with "knowing". Some manuscripts place it after the name, with "saved", which pairs "once" with "the second time". The meaning of the verse hardly changes. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: angels who did not keep their own position: most likely the angels of Genesis 6:1-4, as Jewish tradition told the story
alternatives: the first rebellion of angels against God, before the creation of humankind
decisions.reason: ἀρχὴν means a beginning, and so a rule or a position of authority; οἰκητήριον is a dwelling place (2 Corinthians 5:2). These angels left the rank and home God gave them. Jewish writings of the time, especially 1 Enoch 6-16, told Genesis 6:1-4 as the story of angels ("the sons of God") who left heaven to take human wives and who were bound in darkness until the judgment. Jude quotes 1 Enoch in verses 14-15, and verse 7 says that Sodom sinned "in the same way as these", which fits this story. The text itself names only their desertion and their punishment, as 2 Peter 2:4 does.

decisions.choice: did not keep ... has kept: a play on the same verb
decisions.reason: The angels did not keep (τηρήσαντας) their position, so they are kept (τετήρηκεν) in bonds. It is the verb of verse 1, where the readers are kept for Jesus Christ, and of verses 13 and 21. In the SBLGNT the subject is still the one named in verse 5.

decisions.choice: everlasting bonds under gloom, for the judgment of the great day: a prison of darkness that holds them until the final judgment
decisions.reason: ἀΐδιος means everlasting; it is a different word from the "eternal" of verses 7 and 21, though close in meaning. The bonds hold them until the judgment: the text speaks of where they are held now, as 2 Peter 2:4 does with "chains of gloom". ζόφος is deep, murky darkness, the word of verse 13 and of 2 Peter 2:4 and 17. "The great day" is the day of the Lord's judgment (Joel 2:31; Revelation 6:17).

decisions.choice: Jesus (all levels), with a footnote giving "the Lord" and "God"
decisions.reason: Every level renders the SBLGNT text (m2). The footnote lets readers see the other readings.

decisions.choice: everlasting bonds (L); everlasting chains (B); chains that will last forever (R)
decisions.reason: "Eternal" is kept for the different word in verses 7 and 21 (m8). Balanced and Readable say "chains", the ordinary English for bonds that hold a prisoner.

decisions.choice: deepest darkness (B); in the dark (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:4, Literal says "gloom" and Balanced and Readable say plainly how dark the prison is.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel; the place of authority God had given them
decisions.reason: Readable names the people (m4) and says who gave the angels their place (m6), which the story assumes.

decisions.choice: guardar for τηρέω (verses 1, 6, 13, 21)
decisions.reason: Jude plays on one verb: the readers are kept for Jesus Christ (verse 1), the angels did not keep their position and so are kept in chains (m7), darkness is kept for the false teachers (verse 13), and the readers must keep themselves in God's love (verse 21). Spanish uses "guardar" in each place so the reader can follow the play. Verse 24 has a different verb.

decisions.choice: perpetuas (L, B); que durarán para siempre (R)
decisions.reason: ἀΐδιος is a different word from the "eternal" of verses 7 and 21 (m8). Spanish keeps "eterno" for that word and says "perpetuas" here, as the English keeps "eternal" apart.

decisions.choice: destruyó; los ha guardado (no span)
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun unsaid, so where the English has "he" for Jesus there is often no Spanish word for the deity_pronoun setting to capitalise. Spanish has a span only where a pronoun is written, as in Readable "{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los tiene guardados".

decisions.choice: kulinda for τηρέω (verses 1, 6, 13, 21)
decisions.reason: Jude plays on one verb (m7): the readers are kept (verse 1), the angels did not keep their position and so are kept (verse 6), darkness is kept (verse 13), and the readers must keep themselves (verse 21). Swahili uses "kulinda" in each place where the level keeps the play; verse 24 has a different verb, "kuhifadhi".

decisions.choice: vifungo vya daima (L); minyororo ya daima (B); minyororo itakayodumu milele (R)
decisions.reason: ἀΐδιος is a different word from the "eternal" of verses 7 and 21 (m8). Literal and Balanced keep "milele" for that word and say "daima" (lasting, everlasting) here. Readable says plainly that the chains will last forever, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: n’ont pas gardé ... les a gardés (L, B); perpétuels (L, B)
decisions.reason: French "garder" can carry Jude’s play on one verb (m7), and it is kept for the same verb in verses 1, 13 and 21. "Perpétuels" is used for this word so that "éternel" stays for the different word of verses 7 and 21, as the English keeps "eternal".

decisions.choice: "예수께서" at every level, with the honorific
decisions.reason: The meaning decision follows the SBLGNT, which reads "Jesus", and footnotes the readings "the Lord" and "God"; Korean keeps the name, as the English does, and the meaning decision explains that Jude speaks of Jesus as acting in Israel's history.

decisions.choice: "지키지 않고 ... 지키셨습니다" at every level
decisions.reason: The same Greek verb is used twice, a play on words (meaning decision): the angels did not keep their place, so God has kept them for judgment. Korean repeats "지키다", as the English repeats "keep".

decisions.choice: "이집트"
decisions.reason: "이집트" is the current name, used in the Korean of Matthew and John; "애굽" is the older Protestant form.

decisions.choice: "Đức Giê-xu" at every level
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "Jesus" (m2, uncertain), and the English keeps "Jesus" at every level with a footnote giving "the Lord" and "God"; Vietnamese follows the same text with the honorific the style guide requires.

decisions.choice: "không giữ ... đã giam giữ" (L)
decisions.reason: Jude plays on one verb: the angels did not keep their position, so God has kept them in chains (m7). Literal keeps the echo with "giữ" in both halves.

decisions.choice: cadeias perpétuas (L); correntes perpétuas (B); correntes que vão durar para sempre (R)
decisions.reason: "Eterno" is kept for the different word in verses 7 and 21 (m8), as the English keeps "eternal" there; "perpétuo" says the same lasting quality with another word. The darkness echoes 2 Peter 2:4, "correntes de profunda escuridão".

decisions.choice: ኢየሱስ (Jesus) as the one who saved the people out of Egypt, at every level
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "Jesus" (meaning decision m2), and Jude speaks of Jesus as present and acting in Israel's history (m3); the Amharic keeps the name, as the English does, and does not change it to "the Lord" of other manuscripts.

decisions.choice: ያልጠበቁትን ... ጠብቋቸዋል (who did not keep ... he has kept)
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on one verb (meaning decision m7): the angels did not keep their place, so God keeps them for judgment. Amharic "መጠበቅ" carries both senses, so the play stands at Literal and Balanced, and it links with "kept" in verses 1, 13 and 21.

source.text: ὡς Σόδομα καὶ Γόμορρα καὶ αἱ περὶ αὐτὰς πόλεις, τὸν ὅμοιον τρόπον τούτοις ἐκπορνεύσασαι καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας, πρόκεινται δεῖγμα πυρὸς αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχουσαι.

records.literal_gloss: As Sodom and Gomorrah and the around them cities, the like manner to these having committed sexual immorality and having gone after flesh other, are set forth [as] an example, of fire eternal [the] penalty undergoing.

en.L: So too Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, having committed sexual immorality in the same way as these and having gone after other flesh, are set forth [as] an example, undergoing [the] penalty of eternal fire.
en.B: So too Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns around them, which, like those angels, gave themselves to sexual immorality and went after flesh of another kind, now lie before us as an example, suffering the penalty of eternal fire.
en.R: Think too of Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns around them. Like those angels, the people there were sexually immoral and went after flesh of a different kind. Their punishment by eternal fire is set before everyone as a warning.

es.L: Así también Sodoma y Gomorra y las ciudades de alrededor, que de la misma manera que estos se entregaron a la inmoralidad sexual y fueron tras otra carne, están puestas [como] ejemplo, sufriendo [la] pena del fuego eterno.
es.B: Así también Sodoma y Gomorra y las ciudades vecinas, que, como aquellos ángeles, se entregaron a la inmoralidad sexual y fueron tras carne de otra clase, están ahora ante nosotros como ejemplo, sufriendo la pena del fuego eterno.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} también en Sodoma y Gomorra y en las ciudades vecinas. Igual que aquellos ángeles, la gente de allí vivía en la inmoralidad sexual y fue tras carne de un tipo diferente. Su castigo con fuego eterno está a la vista de todos como advertencia.

sw.L: Kama vile Sodoma na Gomora na miji iliyoizunguka, ambayo kwa namna ileile kama hawa ilijitia katika uasherati na kufuata mwili mwingine, imewekwa mbele [kama] mfano, ikipata adhabu ya moto wa milele.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo Sodoma na Gomora na miji iliyoizunguka, ambayo, kama malaika wale, ilijitia katika uasherati na kufuata mwili wa aina nyingine, sasa iko mbele yetu kama mfano, ikiteseka kwa adhabu ya moto wa milele.
sw.R: Fikirini pia Sodoma na Gomora na miji iliyoizunguka. Kama malaika wale, watu wa huko walifanya uasherati na kufuata mwili wa aina tofauti. Adhabu yao ya moto wa milele imewekwa mbele ya kila mtu kama onyo.

fr.L: De même Sodome et Gomorrhe et les villes d’alentour, s’étant livrées de la même manière que ceux-ci à l’immoralité sexuelle et étant allées après une autre chair, sont proposées en exemple, subissant la peine d’un feu éternel.
fr.B: De même, Sodome et Gomorrhe et les villes voisines, qui, comme ces anges, se sont livrées à l’immoralité sexuelle et sont allées après une chair d’une autre nature, sont maintenant placées devant nous comme un exemple : elles subissent la peine du feu éternel.
fr.R: Pensez aussi à Sodome et Gomorrhe et aux villes voisines. Comme ces anges, les gens de ces villes ont commis des péchés sexuels et sont allés après une chair d’une autre sorte. Leur punition par le feu éternel est placée devant tous comme un avertissement.

ko.L: 소돔과 고모라와 그 주변 도시들도 이들과 같은 방식으로 음행하고 다른 육체를 따라갔으므로, 영원한 불의 형벌을 받아 본보기로 놓여 있습니다.
ko.B: 소돔과 고모라와 그 주변 도시들도 그 천사들처럼 음행에 빠지고 다른 육체를 따라갔으므로, 이제 영원한 불의 형벌을 받는 본보기로 우리 앞에 놓여 있습니다.
ko.R: 소돔과 고모라와 그 주변 도시들도 생각해 보십시오. 그곳 사람들도 그 천사들처럼 음행을 저지르고 다른 육체를 따라갔습니다. 그들이 영원한 불로 받은 형벌은 모든 사람에게 경고로 주어졌습니다.

vi.L: Cũng như Sô-đôm và Gô-mô-rơ và các thành chung quanh, cũng theo cách như những [thiên sứ] ấy, đã phạm tội tà dâm và chạy theo xác thịt khác, được đặt làm gương, chịu hình phạt của lửa đời đời.
vi.B: Cũng vậy, Sô-đôm, Gô-mô-rơ và các thành chung quanh, giống như các thiên sứ ấy, đã buông mình vào sự tà dâm và chạy theo xác thịt khác loại, nay được bày ra trước mắt chúng ta làm gương, chịu hình phạt của lửa đời đời.
vi.R: Cũng hãy nghĩ đến Sô-đôm, Gô-mô-rơ và các thành chung quanh. Giống như các thiên sứ ấy, người ở đó đã phạm tội tà dâm và chạy theo xác thịt khác loại. Hình phạt bằng lửa đời đời của họ được bày ra cho mọi người thấy như một lời cảnh cáo.

pt.L: Assim também Sodoma e Gomorra e as cidades em torno delas, tendo se entregado à imoralidade sexual do mesmo modo que estes e tendo ido atrás de outra carne, estão expostas [como] exemplo, sofrendo [a] pena do fogo eterno.
pt.B: Assim também Sodoma e Gomorra e as cidades vizinhas, que, como aqueles anjos, se entregaram à imoralidade sexual e foram atrás de carne de outro tipo, estão aí diante de nós como exemplo, sofrendo a pena do fogo eterno.
pt.R: Pensem também em Sodoma e Gomorra e nas cidades ao redor delas. Como aqueles anjos, as pessoas dali viviam na imoralidade sexual e foram atrás de carne de um tipo diferente. O castigo delas, com fogo eterno, está diante de todos como um aviso.

am.L: እንደዚሁም ሰዶምና ገሞራ በዙሪያቸውም ያሉት ከተሞች፣ እንደ እነዚህ በተመሳሳይ መንገድ ሴሰኝነትን አድርገው ሌላ ሥጋንም ተከትለው፣ የዘላለምን እሳት ቅጣት እየተቀበሉ ምሳሌ ሆነው ቀርበዋል።
am.B: እንዲሁም ሰዶምና ገሞራ በዙሪያቸውም ያሉት ከተሞች እንደ እነዚያ መላእክት ራሳቸውን ለሴሰኝነት አሳልፈው ሰጡ፤ የሌላ ዓይነት ሥጋንም ተከተሉ። አሁንም የዘላለምን እሳት ቅጣት እየተቀበሉ ለእኛ ምሳሌ ሆነው ቀርበዋል።
am.R: ሰዶምንና ገሞራን በዙሪያቸውም ያሉትን ከተሞች ደግሞ አስቡ። እንደ እነዚያ መላእክት የዚያ ስፍራ ሰዎች ሴሰኞች ነበሩ፤ የሌላ ዓይነት ሥጋንም ተከተሉ። በዘላለም እሳት መቀጣታቸው ለሁሉም ማስጠንቀቂያ ሆኖ ቀርቧል።

decisions.choice: as: a third example, joined to the two in verses 5-6
decisions.reason: ὡς links Sodom and Gomorrah to what comes before: like the unbelieving people and the angels, these cities show what happens to those who rebel. The SBLGNT ends the previous sentence with a raised dot, and this record follows that division.

decisions.choice: Sodom, Gomorrah and the cities around them: destroyed by fire from heaven (Genesis 19:24-29)
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:24-29 tells how fire and sulfur fell on Sodom and Gomorrah; Deuteronomy 29:23 names two of the cities around them, Admah and Zeboiim. The Old Testament and the New hold them up again and again as the great example of judgment (Isaiah 1:9; Matthew 10:15; 2 Peter 2:6).

decisions.choice: in the same way as these: most likely as the angels of verse 6
alternatives: as Sodom and Gomorrah themselves: the cities around sinned as those two did
as the false teachers, who are "these" in verse 8
decisions.reason: τούτοις is masculine or neuter, not feminine like the cities (πόλεις) and the participles that describe them. It most likely points back to the angels of verse 6, the nearest masculine plural. Read that way, Sodom sinned in the same way as the angels: both crossed the boundary between heavenly beings and human beings. Some take it of Sodom and Gomorrah, whose names are neuter in Greek, or of the false teachers.

decisions.choice: went after other flesh: pursued sexual relations outside the bounds God set; the text says "other" or "different" flesh and does not say more
alternatives: sexual relations with angels: the men of Sodom demanded the visitors, who were angels (Genesis 19:1-11)
decisions.reason: ἐκπορνεύω is a strong word for sexual immorality. ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας is literally "after other flesh" or "different flesh". In Genesis 19:1-11 the men of Sodom demanded to have sex with Lot's guests, who were angels, though the men did not know it. If verse 7 compares Sodom with the angels of verse 6 (m3), the point is that both reached across the boundary between angels and humans. Others read "other flesh" as flesh other than what is natural or proper, and so take it of same-sex relations, or of sexual perversion in general; the men of Sodom were demanding sex with other men. Ezekiel 16:49-50 also names Sodom's pride and its neglect of the poor. Jude says that the cities committed sexual immorality and went after "other flesh"; he does not describe the act further.

decisions.choice: set forth as an example, undergoing the penalty of eternal fire
alternatives: an example of eternal fire, undergoing punishment
decisions.reason: πυρὸς αἰωνίου, "of eternal fire", can go with "penalty" (the penalty of eternal fire) or with "example" (an example of eternal fire). Either way the destroyed cities stand as a public warning of the judgment of fire that does not end (2 Peter 2:6). δίκην is a penalty handed down by a judge.

decisions.choice: other flesh (L); flesh of another kind (B); flesh of a different kind (R)
decisions.reason: All three levels keep Jude's own expression and do not choose among the readings (m4).

decisions.choice: like those angels
alternatives: in the same way as these
decisions.reason: "These" has no clear antecedent in English. Balanced and Readable name the angels, the most likely sense (m3).

decisions.choice: set before everyone as a warning
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of example the cities are: a warning of judgment (m5).

decisions.choice: "음행하다" for sexual immorality; "다른 육체를 따라가다" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "went after other flesh" as pursuing sexual relations outside the bounds God set and says the text says "other" or "different" flesh and nothing more, footnoted. Korean keeps the phrase at every level, as the English does, and does not narrow it. "육체" is the body as flesh; "육신" is kept for flesh as fallen nature.

decisions.choice: "xác thịt khác" (L); "xác thịt khác loại" (B, R) for other flesh
decisions.reason: The text says "other" or "different" flesh and does not say more (m4, uncertain), so Vietnamese keeps the phrase as close to the Greek as the English does and adds no explanation.

decisions.choice: "những [thiên sứ] ấy" (L) for "these"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "these" as the angels of verse 6 (m3, uncertain); Vietnamese must name the group, so Literal brackets the word, and Balanced and Readable say it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ሌላ ሥጋን ተከትለው (having gone after other flesh, L); የሌላ ዓይነት ሥጋ (flesh of another kind, B, R)
decisions.reason: The text says "other" or "different" flesh and does not say more (meaning decision m4), so Amharic keeps "ሥጋ" and names no particular sin; the meaning note gives the readings.

source.text: Ὁμοίως μέντοι καὶ οὗτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι σάρκα μὲν μιαίνουσιν, κυριότητα δὲ ἀθετοῦσιν, δόξας δὲ βλασφημοῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Likewise yet also these dreaming [ones] [the] flesh on one hand defile, lordship and reject, glorious [ones] and blaspheme.

en.L: Yet in the same way these also, dreaming, defile the flesh, reject lordship, and blaspheme glorious ones.
en.B: Yet in the same way these dreamers defile their bodies, reject the Lord's authority, and slander the glorious ones.
en.R: These dreamers act in the same way. They make their own bodies unclean with sin. They reject the Lord's authority. And they insult glorious beings in the heavenly world.

es.L: Sin embargo, de la misma manera también estos, soñando, contaminan la carne, rechazan el señorío y blasfeman contra los gloriosos.
es.B: Sin embargo, de la misma manera estos soñadores contaminan su cuerpo, rechazan la autoridad del Señor y calumnian a los seres gloriosos.
es.R: Estos soñadores hacen lo mismo. Hacen impuro su propio cuerpo con el pecado. Rechazan la autoridad del Señor. E insultan a seres gloriosos del mundo celestial.

sw.L: Hata hivyo, vivyo hivyo hawa nao, wakiota ndoto, wanautia mwili unajisi, wanakataa ubwana, na wanawakufuru wenye utukufu.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, vivyo hivyo watu hawa wanaoota ndoto wanaitia miili yao unajisi, wanakataa mamlaka ya Bwana, na wanawatukana wenye utukufu.
sw.R: Watu hawa wanaoota ndoto wanafanya vivyo hivyo. Wanaifanya miili yao kuwa najisi kwa dhambi. Wanakataa mamlaka ya Bwana. Tena wanawatukana viumbe wenye utukufu katika ulimwengu wa mbinguni.

fr.L: Pourtant ceux-ci aussi, de la même manière, en rêvant, souillent la chair, rejettent la seigneurie et blasphèment les gloires.
fr.B: Et pourtant ces rêveurs font de même : ils souillent leur corps, rejettent l’autorité du Seigneur et injurient les êtres glorieux.
fr.R: Ces rêveurs agissent de la même manière. Ils salissent leur propre corps par le péché. Ils rejettent l’autorité du Seigneur. Et ils insultent les êtres glorieux du monde céleste.

ko.L: 그런데 이와 같이 이 꿈꾸는 사람들도 육체를 더럽히고, 주님의 권위를 무시하며, 영광스러운 존재들을 모독합니다.
ko.B: 그런데 이 꿈꾸는 사람들도 마찬가지로 자기 몸을 더럽히고, 주님의 권위를 무시하며, 영광스러운 존재들을 비방합니다.
ko.R: 이 꿈꾸는 사람들도 똑같이 행동합니다. 그들은 죄로 자기 몸을 더럽힙니다. 그들은 주님의 권위를 무시합니다. 그리고 하늘 세계의 영광스러운 존재들을 모욕합니다.

vi.L: Thế mà những kẻ mơ mộng này cũng vậy, làm ô uế xác thịt, khước từ quyền tể trị, và phỉ báng các đấng vinh hiển.
vi.B: Thế mà những kẻ mơ mộng này cũng làm như vậy: họ làm ô uế thân thể mình, khước từ quyền tể trị của Chúa và nói xúc phạm các đấng vinh hiển.
vi.R: Những kẻ chỉ dựa vào giấc mơ này cũng làm như vậy. Họ làm cho thân thể mình ô uế bằng tội lỗi. Họ khước từ quyền tể trị của Chúa. Và họ sỉ nhục những bậc vinh hiển trong thế giới thiên thượng.

pt.L: Contudo, do mesmo modo também estes, sonhando, contaminam a carne, rejeitam o senhorio e blasfemam contra [os] gloriosos.
pt.B: Contudo, da mesma forma esses sonhadores contaminam o próprio corpo, rejeitam a autoridade do Senhor e difamam os seres gloriosos.
pt.R: Esses sonhadores agem do mesmo jeito. Eles tornam o próprio corpo impuro com o pecado. Rejeitam a autoridade do Senhor. E insultam os seres gloriosos do mundo celestial.

am.L: እንደዚሁም ግን እነዚህ ደግሞ እያለሙ ሥጋን ያረክሳሉ፣ ጌትነትንም ይጥላሉ፣ ክቡራንንም ይሳደባሉ።
am.B: ቢሆንም እነዚህ ሕልም አላሚዎች በተመሳሳይ መንገድ ሰውነታቸውን ያረክሳሉ፣ የጌታን ሥልጣን ይጥላሉ፣ ክቡራንንም ይሳደባሉ።
