am.R: እነዚህ ሕልም አላሚዎችም እንደዚሁ ያደርጋሉ። በኃጢአት ሰውነታቸውን ያረክሳሉ። የጌታን ሥልጣን አይቀበሉም። በሰማያዊው ዓለም ያሉትን ክቡራን ፍጡራንም ይሳደባሉ።

decisions.choice: likewise: the false teachers do what the people of verses 5-7 did
decisions.reason: Ὁμοίως, "likewise", with μέντοι, "yet", says that in spite of those warnings these people do the same things: they defile the flesh like Sodom, reject authority like the angels who left their place, and speak against heavenly beings. οὗτοι, "these", is Jude's word for the false teachers through the rest of the letter (verses 10, 12, 16, 19).

decisions.choice: dreaming: they claim visions in dreams as the authority for what they do
alternatives: they live in a dream world, deluded
decisions.reason: ἐνυπνιάζομαι is used of dreams that bring visions (Acts 2:17, quoting Joel 2:28). The Law warns against a prophet or "dreamer of dreams" who leads people away from God (Deuteronomy 13:1-5), and the Greek Old Testament uses this verb there. Jude probably means that they appeal to their own dreams or visions to justify what they do; the word may also describe them as people out of touch with what is real.

decisions.choice: defile the flesh: make their bodies unclean by sexual sin
decisions.reason: The words recall Sodom in verse 7. "Flesh" here is their own body; they defile it by the sexual immorality Jude has described.

decisions.choice: lordship: the Lord's authority
alternatives: angelic powers (the "glorious ones" of the next words)
decisions.reason: κυριότητα comes from the word for lord. Since the false teachers deny "our only Master and Lord" (verse 4), the most likely sense is that they reject the Lord's rule over them. In Ephesians 1:21 and Colossians 1:16 the same word names a rank of spiritual powers, and the next words speak of heavenly beings, so some read it that way. 2 Peter 2:10 has the same pair of ideas.

decisions.choice: glorious ones: heavenly beings, most likely including fallen angels
decisions.reason: δόξας ("glories") is used for angelic beings in Jewish writing, and 2 Peter 2:10 uses it the same way. Verse 9 gives the example: even the archangel Michael did not speak abusively to the devil. So the beings these people mock probably include evil powers, whom they treat with contempt they have no right to.

decisions.choice: blaspheme (L); slander (B); insult (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:10, Literal keeps the Greek word. In current English "blaspheme" is used only of speech against God, so Balanced and Readable use words for abusive speech against others.

decisions.choice: the Lord's authority
decisions.reason: "Lordship" alone is unclear in English; Balanced and Readable say whose authority, as in 2 Peter 2:10 (m4).

decisions.choice: the flesh (L); their bodies (B); their own bodies (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what flesh means here (m3).

decisions.choice: glorious beings in the heavenly world
decisions.reason: Readable says who the glorious ones are, as in 2 Peter 2:10 (m5).

decisions.choice: blasphèment (L); injurient (B); insultent (R), here and in verses 9-10
decisions.reason: As in English, Literal keeps the Greek word; French "blasphémer" is now said only of speech against God or what is sacred, so Balanced and Readable use words for abusive speech (m5). "Calomnier" would mean spreading false reports, which is not the point.

decisions.choice: "주님의 권위"; "영광스러운 존재들" as in 2 Peter 2:10
decisions.reason: The same words as 2 Peter 2:10, with the same Korean; the meaning decisions read lordship as the Lord's authority and the glorious ones as heavenly beings, both footnoted.

decisions.choice: "các đấng vinh hiển" and "phỉ báng" (L), "xúc phạm" (B), "sỉ nhục" (R), as in 2 Peter 2:10-11
decisions.reason: The glorious ones are heavenly beings (m5, uncertain); Vietnamese uses the same words as the parallel passage of the Vietnamese 2 Peter, so the two letters can be read side by side.

decisions.choice: o senhorio, blasfemam contra [os] gloriosos (L); a autoridade do Senhor, difamam os seres gloriosos (B); insultam (R)
decisions.reason: Worded as in 2 Peter 2:10, the parallel verse, so that the two letters read alike where their Greek agrees.

decisions.choice: እያለሙ (dreaming, L), ሕልም አላሚዎች (dreamers, B, R); ክቡራን (glorious ones), ይሳደባሉ (blaspheme, slander), as in the Amharic 2 Peter 2:10
decisions.reason: The false teachers claim visions in dreams as their authority (meaning decision m2). The glorious ones are heavenly beings (m5), and Amharic "ክቡራን" is the word the Amharic 2 Peter uses in its parallel, with "ፍጡራን" (beings) added at Readable.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Μιχαὴλ ὁ ἀρχάγγελος, ὅτε τῷ διαβόλῳ διακρινόμενος διελέγετο περὶ τοῦ Μωϋσέως σώματος, οὐκ ἐτόλμησεν κρίσιν ἐπενεγκεῖν βλασφημίας, ἀλλὰ εἶπεν· Ἐπιτιμήσαι σοι κύριος.

records.literal_gloss: But Michael the archangel, when with the devil disputing he was arguing about the of Moses body, not did dare a judgment to bring of blasphemy, but said: May rebuke you [the] Lord.

en.L: But Michael the archangel, when he was disputing with the devil and arguing about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring against [him] a blasphemous judgment, but said, "[The] Lord rebuke you."
en.B: But when Michael, the archangel, was in a dispute with the devil, arguing over the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against him. Instead he said, "May the Lord rebuke you."
en.R: But think of Michael, the chief angel. He was arguing with the devil about the body of Moses. Yet he did not dare to insult the devil when he accused him. He only said, "May the Lord rebuke you!"

es.L: Pero Miguel el arcángel, cuando, disputando con el diablo, discutía acerca del cuerpo de Moisés, no se atrevió a pronunciar [contra él] un juicio blasfemo, sino que dijo: «[Que el] Señor te reprenda».
es.B: Pero cuando el arcángel Miguel disputaba con el diablo, discutiendo sobre el cuerpo de Moisés, no se atrevió a pronunciar contra él un juicio calumnioso. Al contrario, dijo: «Que el Señor te reprenda».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:piensen|pensad}} en Miguel, el jefe de los ángeles. Él discutía con el diablo sobre el cuerpo de Moisés. Sin embargo, no se atrevió a insultar al diablo cuando lo acusó. Solo le dijo: «¡Que el Señor te reprenda!».

sw.L: Lakini Mikaeli malaika mkuu, alipokuwa akishindana na Ibilisi, akihojiana juu ya mwili wa Musa, hakuthubutu kuleta [juu yake] hukumu ya kukufuru, bali alisema, "Bwana akukemee."
sw.B: Lakini Mikaeli, malaika mkuu, alipokuwa akishindana na Ibilisi, akibishana juu ya mwili wa Musa, hakuthubutu kuleta juu yake hukumu ya matusi. Badala yake alisema, "Bwana akukemee."
sw.R: Lakini fikirini Mikaeli, kiongozi wa malaika. Alikuwa akibishana na Ibilisi kuhusu mwili wa Musa. Hata hivyo, hakuthubutu kumtukana Ibilisi alipomshtaki. Alisema tu, "Bwana akukemee!"

fr.L: Or Michel l’archange, lorsqu’il contestait avec le diable et discutait au sujet du corps de Moïse, n’a pas osé porter [contre lui] un jugement blasphématoire, mais il a dit : « Que le Seigneur te réprimande ! »
fr.B: Pourtant, quand l’archange Michel était en conflit avec le diable et discutait avec lui au sujet du corps de Moïse, il n’a pas osé prononcer contre lui un jugement injurieux. Il a seulement dit : « Que le Seigneur te réprimande ! »
fr.R: Mais pensez à Michel, le chef des anges. Il se disputait avec le diable au sujet du corps de Moïse. Pourtant, il n’a pas osé insulter le diable en l’accusant. Il a seulement dit : « Que le Seigneur te réprimande ! »

ko.L: 그러나 천사장 미가엘은 모세의 시체에 대하여 마귀와 다투며 논쟁할 때에, 감히 모독하는 판결을 내리지 못하고 "주님께서 너를 꾸짖으시기를 [빈다]" 하고 말했습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 천사장 미가엘이 모세의 시체를 두고 마귀와 다투며 논쟁할 때에도, 감히 마귀를 비방하는 판결을 내리지 못하고 "주님께서 너를 꾸짖으시기를 바란다" 하고만 말했습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 천사들의 우두머리인 미가엘을 생각해 보십시오. 미가엘은 모세의 시체를 두고 마귀와 다투었습니다. 그러나 마귀를 고발할 때에도 감히 모욕하지 않았습니다. 그는 "주님께서 너를 꾸짖으실 것이다!" 하고만 말했습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng khi tranh cãi với ma quỷ về thi thể của Môi-se, thiên sứ trưởng Mi-chen cũng không dám đưa ra lời phán xét phỉ báng [nó], nhưng nói: "Nguyện Chúa quở trách ngươi."
vi.B: Nhưng khi thiên sứ trưởng Mi-chen tranh cãi với ma quỷ về thi thể của Môi-se, ông cũng không dám đưa ra lời phán xét xúc phạm nó. Trái lại, ông nói: "Nguyện Chúa quở trách ngươi."
vi.R: Nhưng hãy nghĩ đến Mi-chen, vị thiên sứ trưởng. Ông đã tranh cãi với ma quỷ về thi thể của Môi-se. Thế mà ông cũng không dám sỉ nhục ma quỷ khi buộc tội nó. Ông chỉ nói: "Nguyện Chúa quở trách ngươi!"

pt.L: Mas Miguel, o arcanjo, quando disputava com o diabo, discutindo sobre o corpo de Moisés, não ousou trazer [contra ele] um juízo blasfemo, mas disse: "[O] Senhor repreenda você."
pt.B: Mas Miguel, o arcanjo, quando estava em disputa com o diabo, discutindo sobre o corpo de Moisés, não ousou fazer contra ele uma acusação difamatória. Em vez disso, disse: "Que o Senhor o repreenda."
pt.R: Mas pensem em Miguel, o chefe dos anjos. Ele estava discutindo com o diabo sobre o corpo de Moisés. Mesmo assim, não ousou insultar o diabo quando o acusou. Ele só disse: "Que o Senhor repreenda você!"

am.L: የመላእክት አለቃ ሚካኤል ግን ስለ ሙሴ አካል ከዲያብሎስ ጋር ሲከራከርና ሲነጋገር የስድብ ፍርድ ሊያመጣበት አልደፈረም፤ ነገር ግን «ጌታ ይገሥጽህ» አለ።
am.B: የመላእክት አለቃ ሚካኤል ግን ስለ ሙሴ አካል ከዲያብሎስ ጋር በተከራከረ ጊዜ፣ የስድብ ፍርድ ሊያመጣበት አልደፈረም። ይልቁንም «ጌታ ይገሥጽህ» አለ።
am.R: የመላእክት አለቃ የሆነውን ሚካኤልን አስቡ። እርሱ ስለ ሙሴ አካል ከዲያብሎስ ጋር ይከራከር ነበር። ቢሆንም ዲያብሎስን በከሰሰው ጊዜ ሊሰድበው አልደፈረም። «ጌታ ይገሥጽህ!» ብቻ አለ።

decisions.choice: Michael the archangel: a chief angel, named in Daniel as a protector of Israel
decisions.reason: ἀρχάγγελος means chief angel; the word is used elsewhere in the New Testament only in 1 Thessalonians 4:16. Michael is named in Daniel 10:13, 21 and 12:1 as a great prince who stands for God's people, and in Revelation 12:7 he fights against the dragon.

decisions.choice: the dispute over the body of Moses: a story not found in the Old Testament, which early Christian writers say came from a book called the Assumption of Moses
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 34:5-6 says that Moses died in Moab and was buried there, and that no one knows the place of his grave. The Old Testament says nothing of a dispute between Michael and the devil. Several early Christian writers, among them Clement of Alexandria and Origen, say that Jude took this story from a Jewish book known as the Assumption of Moses. A Jewish work about Moses' last words, usually called the Testament of Moses, survives in one incomplete Latin manuscript; its ending is lost, and the part that survives does not contain the dispute. Whether that work and the Assumption were one book is not certain. Jude tells a story his readers knew; he does not name his source.

decisions.choice: a blasphemous judgment: a condemnation spoken with insult
alternatives: a judgment for blasphemy: he did not pass sentence on the devil's own slander
decisions.reason: κρίσιν ἐπενεγκεῖν βλασφημίας is literally "a judgment of blasphemy". Most likely it means an abusive verdict, an accusation made with insulting words. Michael, though a chief angel, left the verdict to God. The point for Jude's readers is verse 8: the false teachers speak with contempt about heavenly beings, which even Michael did not do to the devil. 2 Peter 2:11 makes the same point without the story.

decisions.choice: The Lord rebuke you: the words spoken to Satan in Zechariah 3:2
decisions.reason: In Zechariah's vision, Satan stands to accuse Joshua the high priest, and the angel of the LORD says, "The LORD rebuke you, Satan." The Hebrew there has the divine name; Jude's Greek has κύριος, "Lord". Ἐπιτιμήσαι is a wish (the optative mood): may the Lord rebuke you. Zechariah 3 comes back in verse 23.

decisions.choice: a blasphemous judgment (L); a slanderous judgment (B); insult ... when he accused him (R)
decisions.reason: The same choice as in verse 8 and 2 Peter 2:11: Literal keeps "blasphemous"; Balanced and Readable use words for abusive speech (m3).

decisions.choice: the chief angel
decisions.reason: Readable says what "archangel" means (m1).

decisions.choice: "미가엘", "천사장"; Michael speaks to the devil in 해라체 ("너를"), with "주님께서" for the Lord
decisions.reason: "미가엘" and "천사장" are the established forms. Michael rebukes an enemy, so he speaks to him in the plain style, and the Lord takes the honorific; the words are those spoken to Satan in Zechariah 3:2 (meaning decision). Readable makes the wish a statement, which is plainer.

decisions.choice: "thiên sứ trưởng Mi-chen", "ông" for Michael, "ngươi" for the devil in his words
decisions.reason: Michael is a chief angel (m1), named in the Protestant form; Vietnamese calls him "ông" with respect. His words to the devil are those spoken to Satan in Zechariah 3:2 (m4), and the solemn "ngươi" fits a rebuke spoken in God's name.

decisions.choice: você (L, R); o (B)
decisions.reason: Michael speaks to the devil, not to God or Jesus, so the ordinary "você" is used, as Jesus addresses Satan in Matthew 4:10 and 16:23; "tu" is kept for addressing God and Christ. Balanced uses the written object pronoun "o" for "você". "Juízo blasfemo" and "acusação difamatória" are the words of 2 Peter 2:11.

decisions.choice: የመላእክት አለቃ ሚካኤል (Michael the archangel); የሙሴ አካል (the body of Moses); ጌታ ይገሥጽህ (the Lord rebuke you)
decisions.reason: "የመላእክት አለቃ" (chief of the angels) is the Amharic title for an archangel, and Michael is well known to Ethiopian readers (meaning decision m1). "አካል" is the body, as the style guide keeps it, here the dead body of Moses. The words of the rebuke are those of Zechariah 3:2 (m4), said with the plain verb "መገሠጽ".

source.text: οὗτοι δὲ ὅσα μὲν οὐκ οἴδασιν βλασφημοῦσιν, ὅσα δὲ φυσικῶς ὡς τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα ἐπίστανται, ἐν τούτοις φθείρονται.

records.literal_gloss: These but, whatever on one hand not they know they blaspheme, whatever but by nature as the irrational animals they understand, in these they are destroyed.

en.L: But these [people] blaspheme the things they do not know; and the things they understand naturally, like irrational animals, in these they are destroyed.
en.B: But these people slander what they know nothing about, while the things they know by instinct, like animals without reason, are the very things that destroy them.
en.R: But these people insult things they know nothing about. They are like wild animals that cannot think. The only things they understand are the things they know by instinct, and those are the very things that destroy them.

es.L: Pero estos blasfeman contra lo que no conocen; y lo que entienden por naturaleza, como los animales irracionales, en eso se destruyen.
es.B: Pero estas personas calumnian lo que no conocen, mientras que lo que conocen por instinto, como animales que no razonan, es precisamente lo que los destruye.
es.R: Pero estas personas insultan cosas que no conocen. Son como animales salvajes que no pueden pensar. Lo único que entienden es lo que saben por instinto, y eso es justamente lo que los destruye.

sw.L: Lakini hawa wanayakufuru mambo wasiyoyajua; na mambo wanayoyaelewa kwa asili, kama wanyama wasio na busara, katika hayo wanaangamizwa.
sw.B: Lakini watu hawa wanatukana mambo wasiyoyajua, na yale wanayoyajua kwa silika, kama wanyama wasioweza kufikiri, ndiyo hasa yanayowaangamiza.
sw.R: Lakini watu hawa wanatukana mambo wasiyoyajua. Wao ni kama wanyama wa porini wasioweza kufikiri. Wanaelewa tu yale wanayoyajua kwa silika, na hayo ndiyo hasa yanayowaangamiza.

fr.L: Mais ceux-ci blasphèment tout ce qu’ils ne connaissent pas, et ce qu’ils savent par nature, comme les animaux sans raison, c’est en cela qu’ils sont détruits.
fr.B: Mais ces gens-là injurient ce qu’ils ne connaissent pas, tandis que ce qu’ils connaissent d’instinct, comme des animaux sans raison, c’est justement cela qui les détruit.
fr.R: Mais ces gens insultent des choses qu’ils ne connaissent pas. Ils sont comme des bêtes sauvages qui ne peuvent pas réfléchir. Les seules choses qu’ils comprennent sont celles qu’ils connaissent par instinct, et ce sont justement elles qui les détruisent.

ko.L: 그러나 이 사람들은 자기들이 알지 못하는 것들은 모독하고, 이성 없는 짐승처럼 본능으로 아는 것들, 그것들로 멸망합니다.
ko.B: 그러나 이 사람들은 자기들이 알지도 못하는 것을 비방하고, 생각할 줄 모르는 짐승처럼 본능으로만 아는 것들, 바로 그것들 때문에 멸망합니다.
ko.R: 그러나 이 사람들은 자기들이 전혀 알지 못하는 것들을 모욕합니다. 그들은 생각할 줄 모르는 들짐승과 같습니다. 그들이 아는 것은 본능으로 아는 것뿐이고, 바로 그것들이 그들을 멸망하게 합니다.

vi.L: Nhưng những kẻ này phỉ báng những điều họ không biết; còn những điều họ hiểu theo bản năng như loài thú vô tri, thì trong những điều ấy họ bị hủy hoại.
vi.B: Nhưng những người này nói xúc phạm những điều họ chẳng hiểu gì, còn những điều họ biết theo bản năng như loài thú không biết suy nghĩ, thì chính những điều đó hủy hoại họ.
vi.R: Nhưng những người này sỉ nhục những điều họ không hiểu gì cả. Họ giống như thú hoang không biết suy nghĩ. Những điều duy nhất họ hiểu là những điều họ biết theo bản năng, và chính những điều đó hủy hoại họ.

pt.L: Mas estes blasfemam contra as coisas que não conhecem; e as coisas que entendem naturalmente, como os animais irracionais, nessas são destruídos.
pt.B: Mas essas pessoas difamam o que não conhecem, enquanto aquilo que conhecem por instinto, como animais que não raciocinam, é justamente o que as destrói.
pt.R: Mas essas pessoas insultam coisas que não conhecem. Elas são como animais selvagens que não conseguem pensar. As únicas coisas que entendem são as que conhecem por instinto, e são justamente essas coisas que as destroem.

am.L: እነዚህ ግን የማያውቁትን ሁሉ ይሳደባሉ፤ አእምሮ እንደሌላቸው እንስሶች በተፈጥሮ በሚያውቁት ሁሉ ግን በዚያ ይጠፋሉ።
am.B: እነዚህ ሰዎች ግን ምንም የማያውቁትን ነገር ይሳደባሉ፤ አእምሮ እንደሌላቸው እንስሶች በደመ ነፍስ የሚያውቋቸው ነገሮች ደግሞ እነርሱኑ ያጠፏቸዋል።
am.R: እነዚህ ሰዎች ግን ምንም የማያውቁትን ነገር ይሳደባሉ። ማሰብ እንደማይችሉ የዱር እንስሶች ናቸው። የሚረዱት በደመ ነፍስ የሚያውቁትን ብቻ ነው፤ እነዚያም ነገሮች እነርሱን ያጠፏቸዋል።

decisions.choice: two kinds of things: what they do not know, and what they know only by instinct
decisions.reason: μὲν and δὲ set two clauses side by side. What they do not know is the spiritual world, the glorious beings of verse 8; what they know by instinct, φυσικῶς, "naturally", like animals, is the life of bodily appetite. They mock the first and are ruined by the second.

decisions.choice: they are destroyed: ruined by the very appetites they follow
decisions.reason: φθείρω can mean to corrupt or to destroy. The parallel in 2 Peter 2:12 says that like animals they will be destroyed, and the examples in verses 5-7 end in destruction, so ruin is most likely meant here.

decisions.choice: a parallel to 2 Peter 2:12
decisions.reason: 2 Peter 2:12 says the same: like irrational animals, born for capture and destruction, they slander what they do not understand and will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: blaspheme (L); slander (B); insult (R)
decisions.reason: The same choice as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: irrational animals (L); animals without reason (B); wild animals that cannot think (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:12.

decisions.choice: አእምሮ እንደሌላቸው እንስሶች (like animals without reason), በደመ ነፍስ (by instinct), with the wording of the Amharic 2 Peter 2:12
decisions.reason: The verse is parallel to 2 Peter 2:12 (meaning decision m3), and where the Greek is the same the Amharic keeps the wording of the Amharic 2 Peter, so the two letters read alike.

source.text: οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς, ὅτι τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Κάϊν ἐπορεύθησαν, καὶ τῇ πλάνῃ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ μισθοῦ ἐξεχύθησαν, καὶ τῇ ἀντιλογίᾳ τοῦ Κόρε ἀπώλοντο.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to them, because in the way of the Cain they went, and to the error of the Balaam for wages they poured themselves out, and in the rebellion of the Korah they perished.

en.L: Woe to them, for they went in the way of Cain, and for wages they poured themselves out into the error of Balaam, and in the rebellion of Korah they perished.
en.B: Woe to them! They have walked in the way of Cain. For the sake of pay they have thrown themselves into the error of Balaam. They have perished in the rebellion of Korah.
en.R: How terrible it will be for them! They have lived like Cain, who killed his brother. They have rushed into the same wrong as Balaam, all for money. And they will be destroyed, just as Korah was when he rebelled against Moses.

es.L: ¡Ay de ellos!, porque anduvieron en el camino de Caín, y por salario se lanzaron al error de Balaam, y en la rebelión de Coré perecieron.
es.B: ¡Ay de ellos! Han seguido el camino de Caín. Por la paga se han lanzado al error de Balaam. Han perecido en la rebelión de Coré.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para ellos! Han vivido como Caín, que mató a su hermano. Se han precipitado en el mismo error que Balaam, y todo por dinero. Y serán destruidos, como Coré cuando se rebeló contra Moisés.

sw.L: Ole wao, kwa sababu walikwenda katika njia ya Kaini, na kwa ajili ya malipo walijimwaga katika upotevu wa Balaamu, na katika uasi wa Kora waliangamia.
sw.B: Ole wao! Wamefuata njia ya Kaini. Kwa ajili ya malipo wamejitosa katika upotevu wa Balaamu. Wameangamia katika uasi wa Kora.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya mno kwao! Wameishi kama Kaini, aliyemuua ndugu yake. Wamekimbilia kosa lilelile la Balaamu, wakitafuta fedha tu. Nao wataangamizwa, kama Kora alivyoangamizwa alipomwasi Musa.

fr.L: Malheur à eux, car ils sont allés dans la voie de Caïn, et pour un salaire ils se sont jetés dans l’égarement de Balaam, et ils ont péri dans la révolte de Coré.
fr.B: Malheur à eux ! Ils ont suivi le chemin de Caïn. Pour de l’argent, ils se sont précipités dans l’égarement de Balaam. Ils ont péri dans la révolte de Coré.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour eux ! Ils ont vécu comme Caïn, qui a tué son frère. Ils se sont précipités dans la même faute que Balaam, et tout cela pour de l’argent. Et ils seront détruits, comme Coré l’a été quand il s’est révolté contre Moïse.

ko.L: 그들에게 화가 있습니다! 그들은 가인의 길을 갔고, 삯을 위해 발람의 잘못에 빠져들었으며, 고라의 반역으로 멸망했습니다.
ko.B: 그들에게 화가 있습니다! 그들은 가인의 길을 걸었고, 돈을 위해 발람의 잘못에 몸을 던졌으며, 고라의 반역으로 멸망했습니다.
ko.R: 그들에게 얼마나 무서운 일이 닥칠지! 그들은 자기 동생을 죽인 가인처럼 살았습니다. 그들은 돈을 위해 발람이 저지른 것과 똑같은 잘못에 뛰어들었습니다. 그리고 모세에게 반역한 고라처럼 멸망할 것입니다.

vi.L: Khốn cho họ, vì họ đã đi theo đường của Ca-in, và vì tiền công mà lao mình vào sự lầm lạc của Ba-la-am, và đã bị hủy diệt trong sự phản loạn của Cô-rê.
vi.B: Khốn cho họ! Họ đã đi theo con đường của Ca-in. Vì tiền công, họ đã lao mình vào sự lầm lạc của Ba-la-am. Họ đã bị hủy diệt trong sự phản loạn của Cô-rê.
vi.R: Thật khủng khiếp cho họ! Họ đã sống như Ca-in, là người đã giết em mình. Họ đã lao vào cùng một điều sai trái như Ba-la-am, tất cả chỉ vì tiền. Và họ sẽ bị hủy diệt, như Cô-rê đã bị hủy diệt khi nổi loạn chống lại Môi-se.

pt.L: Ai deles, porque andaram no caminho de Caim, e por pagamento se precipitaram no erro de Balaão, e pereceram na rebelião de Coré.
pt.B: Ai deles! Andaram no caminho de Caim. Por causa de pagamento, se lançaram no erro de Balaão. Pereceram na rebelião de Coré.
pt.R: Que coisa terrível vai acontecer com eles! Viveram como Caim, que matou o próprio irmão. Correram para o mesmo erro de Balaão, tudo por dinheiro. E vão ser destruídos, assim como Coré foi destruído quando se rebelou contra Moisés.

am.L: ወዮላቸው፤ በቃየል መንገድ ሄደዋልና፤ ስለ ዋጋም በበለዓም ስሕተት ራሳቸውን አፈሰሱ፤ በቆሬም ተቃውሞ ጠፉ።
am.B: ወዮላቸው! በቃየል መንገድ ሄደዋል። ለገንዘብ ብለው ራሳቸውን ወደ በለዓም ስሕተት ወርውረዋል። በቆሬ ዓመፅም ጠፍተዋል።
am.R: ወዮላቸው! እንደ ቃየል ኖረዋል፤ እርሱ ወንድሙን ገደለ። ለገንዘብ ብለው በለዓም ወደ ሠራው ስሕተት ተጣደፉ። ቆሬ በሙሴ ላይ ባመፀ ጊዜ እንደ ጠፋ እነርሱም ይጠፋሉ።

decisions.choice: woe to them: a cry of grief and warning over people facing judgment
decisions.reason: οὐαὶ is the prophets' cry over those who face God's judgment (Isaiah 5:8-22; Habakkuk 2:6-19), and Jesus used it the same way (Matthew 23:13-29). It both mourns and warns.

decisions.choice: the way of Cain: the path of the man who killed his brother
decisions.reason: Cain killed his brother Abel after God had warned him that sin was waiting at his door (Genesis 4:1-16). 1 John 3:12 says Cain belonged to the evil one, and Hebrews 11:4 sets him against Abel's faith. To go in his way is to follow his path.

decisions.choice: the error of Balaam: the prophet who was willing to curse Israel for pay, and who led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: Balaam was hired to curse Israel (Numbers 22-24); afterward his advice led Israel into sexual sin and idolatry at Peor (Numbers 25:1-3; 31:16; compare Revelation 2:14). 2 Peter 2:15 says he "loved the wage of wrongdoing". ἐξεχύθησαν, "they poured themselves out", pictures people rushing headlong into his error for the sake of gain (μισθοῦ).

decisions.choice: the rebellion of Korah: the uprising against Moses and Aaron that ended when the ground swallowed the rebels
decisions.reason: Korah led a revolt against the leadership God had given through Moses and Aaron, and he and his followers perished (Numbers 16:1-35). ἀντιλογίᾳ means speaking against, and so rebellion.

decisions.choice: three past tenses: their end is spoken of as already settled
decisions.reason: The three verbs are aorists, the tense of a completed act. The first two describe what they have done. The third, ἀπώλοντο, "they perished", speaks of their destruction as if it had already happened, because it is as certain as Korah's.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for them
decisions.reason: "Woe" is no longer ordinary English. Literal and Balanced keep the prophets' cry; Readable says what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: who killed his brother; all for money; when he rebelled against Moses
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader who the three men were (m2-m4).

decisions.choice: they perished (L); they have perished (B); they will be destroyed, just as Korah was (R)
decisions.reason: All three levels say that their end is certain (m5); Readable says it as a future, which is what the past tense means here.

decisions.choice: Caïn, Balaam, Coré
decisions.reason: The usual French forms of the three names (m2-m4). "Malheur à eux" is still current French for the prophets’ cry (m1), so only Readable recasts it.

decisions.choice: "화가 있습니다" (L, B), the "woe" of the Korean Gospels in the letter's 합쇼체; "가인", "발람", "고라"
decisions.reason: Woe is a cry of grief and warning over people facing judgment (meaning decision). The Korean Gospels say "화가 있다"; here it takes the letter's 합쇼체. Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does, and gives each name its story.

decisions.choice: "멸망할 것입니다" (R) for the past tense "perished"
decisions.reason: The three past tenses speak of their end as already settled (meaning decision). Literal and Balanced keep the past; Readable, which explains the stories, says "will be destroyed", as the English Readable does, so that a reader does not think the false teachers are already dead.

decisions.choice: "Khốn cho họ" (L, B) for woe to them
decisions.reason: Woe is a cry of grief and warning over people facing judgment (m1); "khốn cho" is the Vietnamese church form of that cry. Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does. "Cô-rê" is the Protestant form of Korah.

decisions.choice: se precipitaram (L); se lançaram (B)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures liquid poured out, people abandoning themselves to Balaam's error (m3). "Derramar-se" would read oddly in Portuguese; "precipitar-se" and "lançar-se" keep the headlong rush. Names in their Brazilian form: Caim, Balaão (as in 2 Peter 2:15), Coré.

decisions.choice: ወዮላቸው (woe to them); ቃየል (Cain), በለዓም (Balaam), ቆሬ (Korah); past tenses at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: "ወዮላቸው" is the table's "woe", a cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m1). The names are as Amharic readers know them, with "ቃየል" as in 1 John 3:12 and "በለዓም" as in the Amharic 2 Peter 2:15. The three past tenses speak of their end as already settled (m5), and Literal and Balanced keep them; "ዋጋ" is the style guide's word for this Greek word for pay.

source.text: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες συνευωχούμενοι, ἀφόβως ἑαυτοὺς ποιμαίνοντες, νεφέλαι ἄνυδροι ὑπὸ ἀνέμων παραφερόμεναι, δένδρα φθινοπωρινὰ ἄκαρπα δὶς ἀποθανόντα ἐκριζωθέντα, κύματα ἄγρια θαλάσσης ἐπαφρίζοντα τὰς ἑαυτῶν αἰσχύνας, ἀστέρες πλανῆται οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους εἰς αἰῶνα τετήρηται.

records.literal_gloss: These are the [ones] in the love feasts of you reefs, feasting together fearlessly, themselves shepherding, clouds waterless by winds being carried along, trees late-autumn fruitless, twice having died, having been uprooted, \v 13 waves wild of [the] sea foaming up the of themselves shames, stars wandering, for whom the gloom of the darkness to [the] age has been kept.

en.L: These are the ones [who are] reefs in your love feasts, feasting together fearlessly, shepherding themselves; clouds without water, carried along by winds; trees of late autumn, fruitless, twice dead, uprooted; \v 13 wild waves of [the] sea, foaming up their own shames; wandering stars, for whom the gloom of darkness has been kept forever.
en.B: At your love feasts these people are like reefs hidden under the water. They eat with you without a trace of fear, shepherds who look after only themselves. They are clouds that bring no rain, blown along by the winds; trees in late autumn with no fruit, twice dead and pulled up by the roots; \v 13 wild waves of the sea, churning up their shameful deeds like foam; wandering stars, for whom the blackest darkness has been kept forever.
en.R: These people are like hidden rocks under the water that wreck ships. They are there at your love feasts, the meals where you eat together. They eat with you and are not afraid of anything. They take care of no one but themselves. They are like clouds that bring no rain and are blown along by the wind. They are like trees at the end of autumn that have no fruit. They are dead twice over, pulled out roots and all. \v 13 They are like wild waves in the sea, throwing up their shameful deeds like foam. They are like stars that wander off course. A place of deep darkness is being kept ready for them forever.

es.L: Estos son los que son arrecifes en los banquetes de amor {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestros}}, banqueteando juntos sin temor, apacentándose a sí mismos; nubes sin agua, llevadas por los vientos; árboles de fines del otoño, sin fruto, dos veces muertos, arrancados de raíz; \v 13 olas salvajes del mar, que echan la espuma de sus propias vergüenzas; estrellas errantes, para quienes la oscuridad de las tinieblas ha sido guardada para siempre.
es.B: En los banquetes de amor {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestros}} estas personas son como arrecifes ocultos bajo el agua. Comen con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sin el menor temor, pastores que solo cuidan de sí mismos. Son nubes que no traen lluvia, llevadas por los vientos; árboles a fines del otoño sin fruto, dos veces muertos y arrancados de raíz; \v 13 olas salvajes del mar que arrojan como espuma sus hechos vergonzosos; estrellas errantes, para quienes está guardada para siempre la más negra oscuridad.
es.R: Estas personas son como rocas escondidas bajo el agua, que hacen naufragar los barcos. Están presentes en los banquetes de amor {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestros}}, las comidas en que {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} juntos. Comen con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y no tienen miedo de nada. No cuidan de nadie más que de sí mismos. Son como nubes que no traen lluvia y que el viento se lleva. Son como árboles al final del otoño, que no tienen fruto. Están muertos dos veces, arrancados con raíz y todo. \v 13 Son como olas salvajes del mar, que arrojan como espuma sus hechos vergonzosos. Son como estrellas que se salen de su camino. Un lugar de oscuridad profunda está guardado para ellos por siempre.

sw.L: Hawa ndio wale walio miamba katika karamu zenu za upendo, wakila karamu pamoja [nanyi] bila hofu, wakijichunga wenyewe; mawingu yasiyo na maji, yakichukuliwa na pepo; miti ya mwishoni mwa vuli, isiyo na matunda, iliyokufa mara mbili, iliyong'olewa; \v 13 mawimbi makali ya bahari, yakirusha povu la aibu zao wenyewe; nyota zinazotangatanga, ambazo kwa ajili yao utusitusi wa giza umelindwa milele.
sw.B: Katika karamu zenu za upendo watu hawa ni kama miamba iliyojificha chini ya maji. Wanakula pamoja nanyi bila hofu yoyote, wachungaji wanaojilisha wenyewe tu. Ni mawingu yasiyoleta mvua, yanayopeperushwa na upepo; miti ya mwishoni mwa vuli isiyo na matunda, iliyokufa mara mbili na kung'olewa na mizizi yake; \v 13 mawimbi makali ya bahari, yanayotoa matendo yao ya aibu kama povu; nyota zinazotangatanga, ambazo kwa ajili yao giza jeusi kabisa limewekwa milele.
sw.R: Watu hawa ni kama miamba iliyojificha chini ya maji inayovunja meli. Wako katika karamu zenu za upendo, yaani milo mnayokula pamoja. Wanakula pamoja nanyi bila kuogopa chochote. Hawamjali mtu yeyote ila wao wenyewe. Ni kama mawingu yasiyoleta mvua yanayopeperushwa na upepo. Ni kama miti isiyo na matunda yoyote wakati wa mavuno. Imekufa mara mbili, imeng'olewa pamoja na mizizi yake. \v 13 Ni kama mawimbi makali ya bahari, yanayotupa matendo yao ya aibu kama povu. Ni kama nyota zinazotoka nje ya njia yao. Mahali pa giza nene pameandaliwa kwa ajili yao milele.

fr.L: Ce sont eux qui, dans vos agapes, [sont] des écueils, festoyant avec vous sans crainte, se paissant eux-mêmes ; nuées sans eau, emportées par les vents ; arbres de fin d’automne, sans fruits, deux fois morts, déracinés ; \v 13 vagues sauvages de la mer, rejetant l’écume de leurs propres hontes ; astres errants, à qui l’obscurité des ténèbres a été gardée pour toujours.
fr.B: Dans vos agapes, ces gens sont comme des écueils cachés sous l’eau. Ils mangent avec vous sans la moindre crainte, des bergers qui ne prennent soin que d’eux-mêmes. Ce sont des nuages sans pluie, poussés par les vents ; des arbres de fin d’automne sans fruits, deux fois morts et arrachés avec leurs racines ; \v 13 des vagues sauvages de la mer, qui rejettent leurs actes honteux comme de l’écume ; des étoiles errantes, à qui les ténèbres les plus noires sont réservées pour toujours.
fr.R: Ces gens sont comme des rochers cachés sous l’eau, qui font couler les bateaux. Ils sont là à vos agapes, les repas où vous mangez ensemble. Ils mangent avec vous et n’ont peur de rien. Ils ne s’occupent de personne d’autre qu’eux-mêmes. Ils sont comme des nuages qui n’apportent pas de pluie et que le vent emporte. Ils sont comme des arbres à la fin de l’automne, qui n’ont pas de fruits. Ils sont morts deux fois, arrachés avec toutes leurs racines. \v 13 Ils sont comme des vagues sauvages de la mer, qui rejettent leurs actes honteux comme de l’écume. Ils sont comme des étoiles qui s’égarent loin de leur route. Un lieu de profondes ténèbres leur est réservé pour toujours.

ko.L: 이 사람들은 여러분의 애찬에서 [숨은] 암초들이며, 두려움 없이 함께 먹으며 자기만 돌보는 목자들이고, 바람에 밀려가는 물 없는 구름이며, 늦가을에 열매 없이 두 번 죽고 뿌리째 뽑힌 나무들이고, \v 13 자기들의 수치를 거품처럼 뿜어내는 바다의 거친 물결이며, 길 잃은 별들입니다. 그들을 위해 캄캄한 어둠이 영원히 준비되어 있습니다.
ko.B: 이 사람들은 여러분의 애찬에서 물 밑에 숨은 암초와 같습니다. 그들은 조금도 두려워하지 않고 여러분과 함께 먹으며, 자기만 돌보는 목자들입니다. 그들은 바람에 밀려가는 비 없는 구름이고, 늦가을에 열매가 없어 두 번 죽고 뿌리째 뽑힌 나무입니다. \v 13 그들은 자기들의 부끄러운 행실을 거품처럼 뿜어 올리는 바다의 거친 물결이고, 길을 잃고 떠도는 별들입니다. 그들을 위해 가장 캄캄한 어둠이 영원히 준비되어 있습니다.
ko.R: 이 사람들은 물 밑에 숨어 있어서 배를 부수는 바위와 같습니다. 그들은 여러분이 함께 먹는 식사인 애찬에 함께합니다. 그들은 여러분과 함께 먹으면서 아무것도 두려워하지 않습니다. 그들은 자기 자신만 돌봅니다. 그들은 비를 내리지 않고 바람에 날려 가는 구름과 같습니다. 그들은 늦가을에 열매가 하나도 없는 나무와 같습니다. 두 번 죽은 것이고, 뿌리째 뽑혔습니다. \v 13 그들은 바다의 거친 물결과 같아서, 자기들의 부끄러운 행실을 거품처럼 뿜어 올립니다. 그들은 제 길을 벗어나 떠도는 별과 같습니다. 그들을 위해 깊은 어둠의 자리가 영원히 준비되어 있습니다.

vi.L: Những kẻ này là đá ngầm trong các bữa tiệc yêu thương của anh chị em, cùng ăn tiệc không chút sợ hãi, chỉ chăn chính mình; là mây không nước, bị gió đưa đi đây đó; là cây cuối thu không trái, chết hai lần, bị nhổ rễ; \v 13 là sóng dữ ngoài biển, sủi bọt ra những điều sỉ nhục của mình; là những ngôi sao lang thang, là những kẻ mà sự tối tăm mù mịt đã được dành sẵn cho đời đời.
vi.B: Trong các bữa tiệc yêu thương của anh chị em, những người này giống như đá ngầm dưới mặt nước. Họ ăn uống với anh chị em mà không chút sợ hãi, như những người chăn chỉ lo cho chính mình. Họ là những đám mây không đem mưa, bị gió cuốn đi; là những cây cuối thu không có trái, chết hai lần và bị nhổ tận gốc; \v 13 là những đợt sóng dữ ngoài biển khơi, sủi bọt ra những việc làm đáng hổ thẹn của mình; là những ngôi sao lang thang, mà sự tối tăm dày đặc nhất đã được dành sẵn cho đời đời.
vi.R: Những người này giống như những tảng đá ngầm dưới nước làm đắm tàu. Họ có mặt trong các bữa tiệc yêu thương của anh chị em, là những bữa ăn anh chị em cùng ăn với nhau. Họ ăn với anh chị em mà chẳng sợ gì cả. Họ không lo cho ai ngoài chính mình. Họ giống như những đám mây không đem mưa, bị gió thổi đi. Họ giống như những cây cuối mùa thu không có trái. Họ chết đến hai lần, bị nhổ lên cả rễ. \v 13 Họ giống như những đợt sóng dữ ngoài biển, tung lên những việc làm đáng hổ thẹn của mình như bọt nước. Họ giống như những ngôi sao đi lạc khỏi đường của mình. Một nơi tối tăm mịt mù đang được dành sẵn cho họ đời đời.

pt.L: Estes são os [que são] recifes nas festas de amor de vocês, banqueteando-se juntos sem temor, apascentando a si mesmos; nuvens sem água, levadas pelos ventos; árvores do fim do outono, sem fruto, duas vezes mortas, arrancadas pela raiz; \v 13 ondas bravias do mar, espumando as suas próprias vergonhas; estrelas errantes, para as quais a escuridão das trevas está guardada para sempre.
pt.B: Nas festas de amor de vocês, essas pessoas são como recifes escondidos debaixo da água. Comem com vocês sem nenhum temor, pastores que só cuidam de si mesmos. São nuvens que não trazem chuva, levadas pelos ventos; árvores no fim do outono, sem fruto, duas vezes mortas e arrancadas pela raiz; \v 13 ondas bravias do mar, lançando como espuma as suas ações vergonhosas; estrelas errantes, para as quais a escuridão mais negra está guardada para sempre.
pt.R: Essas pessoas são como rochas escondidas debaixo da água, que afundam navios. Elas estão presentes nas festas de amor de vocês, as refeições em que vocês comem juntos. Comem com vocês e não têm medo de nada. Não cuidam de ninguém, só de si mesmas. São como nuvens que não trazem chuva e são levadas pelo vento. São como árvores no fim do outono que não têm fruto. Estão mortas duas vezes, arrancadas com raiz e tudo. \v 13 São como ondas bravias do mar, que lançam as suas ações vergonhosas como espuma. São como estrelas que saem do seu caminho. Um lugar de profunda escuridão está sendo guardado para elas para sempre.

am.L: እነዚህ በፍቅር ማዕዶቻችሁ [የተሰወሩ] ዓለቶች ናቸው፤ ያለ ፍርሃት አብረው ይበላሉ፤ ራሳቸውን ያሰማራሉ፤ በነፋሳት የሚነዱ ውኃ የሌላቸው ደመናዎች፤ ፍሬ የሌላቸው፣ ሁለት ጊዜ የሞቱ፣ ከሥር የተነቀሉ የመከር መጨረሻ ዛፎች፤ \v 13 የራሳቸውን ነውር አረፋ አድርገው የሚያወጡ የባሕር ጨካኝ ማዕበሎች፤ የጨለማው ጽልመት ለዘላለም የተጠበቀላቸው የሚቅበዘበዙ ከዋክብት [ናቸው]።
am.B: እነዚህ ሰዎች በፍቅር ማዕዳችሁ ላይ በውኃ ውስጥ እንደ ተሰወሩ ዓለቶች ናቸው። ያለ ምንም ፍርሃት ከእናንተ ጋር ይበላሉ፤ ራሳቸውን ብቻ የሚጠብቁ እረኞች ናቸው። በነፋስ የሚነዱ ዝናብ የማያመጡ ደመናዎች ናቸው፤ በመከር ወራት መጨረሻ ፍሬ የሌላቸው፣ ሁለት ጊዜ የሞቱና ከሥራቸው የተነቀሉ ዛፎች ናቸው፤ \v 13 አሳፋሪ ሥራቸውን እንደ አረፋ የሚደፍቁ ጨካኝ የባሕር ማዕበሎች፣ ድቅድቅ ጨለማ ለዘላለም የተጠበቀላቸው የሚቅበዘበዙ ከዋክብት ናቸው።
am.R: እነዚህ ሰዎች መርከቦችን የሚሰብሩ በውኃ ውስጥ የተሰወሩ ዓለቶችን ይመስላሉ። በፍቅር ማዕዳችሁ፣ ማለትም አብራችሁ በምትበሉበት ማዕድ፣ ይገኛሉ። ከእናንተ ጋር ይበላሉ፤ ምንም አይፈሩም። ከራሳቸው በቀር ማንንም አይንከባከቡም። ዝናብ እንደማያመጡና በነፋስ እንደሚነዱ ደመናዎች ናቸው። በመከር ወራት መጨረሻ ፍሬ እንደሌላቸው ዛፎች ናቸው። ሁለት ጊዜ ሞተዋል፤ ከሥራቸውም ተነቅለዋል። \v 13 አሳፋሪ ሥራቸውን እንደ አረፋ የሚደፍቁ ጨካኝ የባሕር ማዕበሎችን ይመስላሉ። መንገዳቸውን ስተው እንደሚቅበዘበዙ ከዋክብት ናቸው። ድቅድቅ ጨለማ ያለበት ስፍራ ለዘላለም ተዘጋጅቶላቸዋል።

decisions.choice: reefs: rocks hidden under the surface, on which ships are wrecked
decisions.reason: σπιλάς normally means a rock in or under the sea, a reef. A word that sounds much the same, σπίλος, means a stain or spot, and 2 Peter 2:13, the parallel verse, calls the false teachers "stains and blemishes". Some read Jude's word in that sense too, but the usual meaning gives a clear picture: like rocks hidden under calm water, these people make the church's meals dangerous for anyone who comes near.

decisions.choice: love feasts: the church's shared meals
decisions.reason: ἀγάπαις is the plural of the word for love. Here it names the common meals of the early churches, which could include the Lord's Supper (Acts 2:46; 1 Corinthians 11:20-34). συνευωχούμενοι, "feasting together", is the word 2 Peter 2:13 uses. The false teachers were not outsiders; they sat at the same table.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "love feasts"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ἀγάπαις, "love feasts". Some manuscripts read a word that differs by a few letters and means "deceptions". In 2 Peter 2:13 the situation is reversed: the SBLGNT reads "deceptions" there, and some manuscripts read "love feasts". Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: shepherding themselves: leaders who care only for themselves
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 34:2-10 condemns the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves instead of the flock. ἀφόβως, "fearlessly", means without reverence for God or without shame.

decisions.choice: four pictures from nature: they promise much and give nothing, and their end is ruin
decisions.reason: Clouds that bring no rain promise what they never give (Proverbs 25:14). Trees in late autumn, the time of harvest, should have fruit and have none. Wild waves throw foam and refuse onto the shore; Isaiah 57:20 compares the wicked to the tossing sea, whose waters cast up mire and mud. Wandering stars leave their proper course; 1 Enoch 18:13-16 and 21:1-6 describe stars bound in punishment for not keeping their appointed times, and that may be Jude's background, as 1 Enoch is in verses 6 and 14. The pictures move through air, earth, sea and sky.

decisions.choice: twice dead, uprooted: dead because fruitless, and dead again because pulled up, beyond any hope of growth
alternatives: dead in this life and dead in the judgment (the second death, Revelation 20:14)
decisions.reason: δὶς, "twice", is not explained. Most likely the tree is dead once in bearing no fruit and dead again in being uprooted. Some see a reference to the second death of Revelation 20:14.

decisions.choice: the gloom of darkness kept forever: the place of punishment, already reserved for them
decisions.reason: 2 Peter 2:17 has the same words, without "forever". The verb is the "keep" of verses 1, 6 and 21: the darkness is kept for them as the readers are kept for Jesus Christ.

decisions.choice: reefs (L); reefs hidden under the water (B); hidden rocks under the water that wreck ships (R)
decisions.reason: Literal gives the word; Balanced and Readable explain the danger it pictures (m1).

decisions.choice: the meals where you eat together
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a love feast was (m2).

decisions.choice: like (B, R)
decisions.reason: The pictures are metaphors. Balanced adds "like" for the first picture; Readable adds it for each, which makes clear that they are comparisons.

decisions.choice: the blackest darkness (B); a place of deep darkness (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:17 (m7).

decisions.choice: los banquetes de amor {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestros}}
decisions.reason: With ustedes, "sus banquetes" could be read as the false teachers' meals. "De ustedes" makes clear that the love feasts are the readers' own church meals (m2), as in 2 Peter 2:13.

decisions.choice: mwishoni mwa vuli (L, B); wakati wa mavuno (R)
decisions.reason: "Vuli" is the standard Swahili word for autumn, but in East Africa it also names the season of the short rains, which is not a harvest time. The point of the picture is a tree with no fruit when fruit is expected (m5), so Readable says "wakati wa mavuno" (harvest time). A reviewer should check that "vuli" is clear to readers.

decisions.choice: vos agapes (every level), explained at Readable
decisions.reason: "Agape" is the French name, taken from the Greek word, for the church’s shared meals (m2), and it keeps the link with the word for love; Readable says what they were.

decisions.choice: des écueils (L); des écueils cachés sous l’eau (B); des rochers cachés sous l’eau, qui font couler les bateaux (R)
decisions.reason: The word means rocks hidden under the surface (m1). "Écueil" is the French word for such a rock, and it already carries the idea of hidden danger; Balanced and Readable say more.

decisions.choice: "애찬" for the love feasts; "암초" for reefs
decisions.reason: The love feasts are the church's shared meals (meaning decision); "애찬" is the established church word, which Readable explains. The meaning decision reads the other word as reefs, rocks hidden under the surface, and footnotes the reading "blemishes" (2 Peter 2:13); Korean follows the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: "bữa tiệc yêu thương" for the love feasts
decisions.reason: The love feasts are the church's shared meals (m2), named with the word for love used through these letters; "tiệc thánh" is the Lord's Supper and would narrow it.

decisions.choice: "đá ngầm" for the reefs (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as rocks hidden under the surface, on which ships are wrecked (m1, uncertain); "vết nhơ" (stains), the other reading, is the word of 2 Peter 2:13.

decisions.choice: as festas de amor
decisions.reason: "Festas de amor" keeps the word "love" that names the meals (m2) and is understood without church knowledge; "ágape" is known only to some readers. Readable explains what the meals were, as the English Readable does. "A escuridão das trevas" (L) and "a escuridão mais negra" (B) as in 2 Peter 2:17.

decisions.choice: የፍቅር ማዕድ (love feast); [የተሰወሩ] ዓለቶች (hidden reefs); የመከር መጨረሻ ዛፎች (trees at the end of harvest time), for "late autumn"
decisions.reason: The love feasts are the church's shared meals (meaning decision m2), and "ማዕድ" is a shared table. The reefs are rocks hidden under the water (m1), which Literal brackets and Balanced and Readable explain. The Greek season is the end of the fruit harvest, when fruit is expected; Ethiopian seasons do not match the Mediterranean ones ("በልግ" is the short rains), so Amharic names the harvest, which keeps the point that the trees are fruitless when fruit is due.

source.text: Προεφήτευσεν δὲ καὶ τούτοις ἕβδομος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ Ἑνὼχ λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν κύριος ἐν ἁγίαις μυριάσιν αὐτοῦ, ποιῆσαι κρίσιν κατὰ πάντων καὶ ἐλέγξαι πάντας τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς περὶ πάντων τῶν ἔργων ἀσεβείας αὐτῶν ὧν ἠσέβησαν καὶ περὶ πάντων τῶν σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀσεβεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Prophesied and also to these [the] seventh from Adam Enoch, saying: Look, came [the] Lord with holy myriads of him, \v 15 to do judgment against all and to convict all the ungodly concerning all the works of ungodliness of them which they did ungodly and concerning all the hard [things] which spoke against him sinners ungodly.

en.L: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied about these, saying, "Look, [the] Lord came with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy myriads, \v 15 to execute judgment against all, and to convict all the ungodly concerning all their works of ungodliness that they did in ungodliness, and concerning all the hard words that ungodly sinners spoke against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: Enoch, the seventh in line from Adam, also prophesied about these people. He said, "Look! The Lord is coming with tens of thousands of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones \v 15 to bring judgment on everyone, and to prove all the ungodly guilty of every ungodly deed they have done in their ungodliness, and of every hard word spoken against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by ungodly sinners."
en.R: Enoch was the seventh in the family line that began with Adam. He also spoke a prophecy about these people. He said, "Look! The Lord will come with many thousands of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy angels. \v 15 He will judge everyone. He will show that all the ungodly are guilty of all the ungodly things they have done. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show that they are guilty of all the hard and cruel words that ungodly sinners have said against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: Y también de estos profetizó Enoc, el séptimo desde Adán, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, vino [el] Señor con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} santas miríadas, \v 15 para hacer juicio contra todos y para dejar convictos a todos los impíos de todas sus obras de impiedad que hicieron impíamente, y de todas las cosas duras que hablaron contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pecadores impíos».
es.B: Enoc, el séptimo en la descendencia de Adán, también profetizó acerca de estas personas. Dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! El Señor viene con decenas de miles de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} santos \v 15 para juzgar a todos, y para demostrar que todos los impíos son culpables de todas las obras impías que han cometido en su impiedad, y de todas las palabras duras que los pecadores impíos han dicho contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».
es.R: Enoc era el séptimo en la línea familiar que comenzó con Adán. Él también dio una profecía acerca de estas personas. Dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! El Señor vendrá con muchos miles de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} santos ángeles. \v 15 Juzgará a todos. Demostrará que todos los impíos son culpables de todas las cosas impías que han hecho. Y demostrará que son culpables de todas las palabras duras y crueles que los pecadores impíos han dicho contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».

sw.L: Na Henoko, wa saba kutoka kwa Adamu, alitoa unabii pia juu ya hawa, akisema, "Tazama, Bwana alikuja pamoja na makumi ya maelfu ya watakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, \v 15 kufanya hukumu juu ya wote, na kuwathibitishia hatia wote wasiomcha Mungu kuhusu matendo yao yote ya kutomcha Mungu waliyoyatenda kwa kutomcha Mungu, na kuhusu maneno yote magumu ambayo wenye dhambi wasiomcha Mungu walisema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."
sw.B: Henoko, wa saba katika ukoo kutoka kwa Adamu, alitoa unabii pia kuhusu watu hawa. Alisema, "Tazama! Bwana anakuja pamoja na makumi ya maelfu ya watakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} \v 15 ili kuwahukumu wote, na kuwathibitishia hatia wote wasiomcha Mungu kwa kila tendo la kutomcha Mungu walilotenda katika kutomcha Mungu kwao, na kwa kila neno gumu ambalo wenye dhambi wasiomcha Mungu wamesema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."
sw.R: Henoko alikuwa wa saba katika ukoo ulioanza na Adamu. Yeye pia alitoa unabii kuhusu watu hawa. Alisema, "Tazama! Bwana atakuja pamoja na maelfu mengi ya malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} watakatifu. \v 15 Atawahukumu watu wote. Ataonyesha kwamba wote wasiomcha Mungu wana hatia kwa mambo yote ya kutomcha Mungu waliyoyafanya. Tena ataonyesha kwamba wana hatia kwa maneno yote magumu na ya kikatili ambayo wenye dhambi wasiomcha Mungu wamesema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."

fr.L: Hénoch aussi, le septième depuis Adam, a prophétisé à leur sujet, disant : « Voici, le Seigneur est venu avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saintes myriades, \v 15 pour exercer le jugement contre tous et pour convaincre tous les impies de toutes les œuvres d’impiété qu’ils ont commises dans leur impiété, et de toutes les paroles dures que des pécheurs impies ont proférées contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »
fr.B: Hénoch, le septième dans la lignée d’Adam, a aussi prophétisé au sujet de ces gens. Il a dit : « Voici que le Seigneur vient avec des dizaines de milliers de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saints \v 15 pour exercer le jugement sur tous, et pour prouver la culpabilité de tous les impies, pour toutes les œuvres impies qu’ils ont commises dans leur impiété, et pour toutes les paroles dures que des pécheurs impies ont prononcées contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »
fr.R: Hénoch était le septième dans la famille qui a commencé avec Adam. Lui aussi a prononcé une prophétie au sujet de ces gens. Il a dit : « Regardez ! Le Seigneur viendra avec des milliers et des milliers de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saints anges. \v 15 Il jugera tout le monde. Il montrera que tous les impies sont coupables de toutes les choses impies qu’ils ont faites. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} montrera qu’ils sont coupables de toutes les paroles dures et cruelles que des pécheurs impies ont dites contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »

ko.L: 아담의 칠 대손 에녹도 이 사람들에 대하여 예언하여 말했습니다. "보아라, 주님께서 수만 명의 거룩한 자들과 함께 오셨다. \v 15 모든 사람을 심판하시고, 경건하지 않은 모든 사람이 경건하지 않게 행한 모든 경건하지 않은 행위와, 경건하지 않은 죄인들이 그분을 거슬러 한 모든 거친 말에 대하여 그들의 죄를 드러내시려는 것이다."
ko.B: 아담의 칠 대손 에녹도 이 사람들에 대해 예언하여 말했습니다. "보아라! 주님께서 수만 명의 거룩한 천사들과 함께 오신다. \v 15 모든 사람을 심판하시고, 경건하지 않은 사람들이 경건하지 않게 행한 모든 경건하지 않은 일과, 경건하지 않은 죄인들이 주님을 거슬러 한 모든 거친 말에 대해 그들의 죄를 밝히시려는 것이다."
ko.R: 에녹은 아담에서 시작된 집안의 일곱째 사람이었습니다. 에녹도 이 사람들에 대해 예언하여 말했습니다. "보아라! 주님께서 수많은 거룩한 천사들과 함께 오실 것이다. \v 15 주님께서는 모든 사람을 심판하실 것이다. 하나님을 공경하지 않는 모든 사람이 하나님을 공경하지 않고 저지른 모든 일에 대해 그들이 죄가 있다는 것을 밝히실 것이다. 하나님을 공경하지 않는 죄인들이 주님을 거슬러 한 모든 거칠고 잔인한 말에 대해서도 그들이 죄가 있다는 것을 밝히실 것이다."

vi.L: Và Hê-nóc, người thứ bảy kể từ A-đam, cũng đã nói tiên tri về những kẻ này rằng: "Kìa, Chúa đã đến với muôn vạn đấng thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 15 để thi hành sự phán xét trên mọi người, và để buộc tội mọi kẻ không tin kính về mọi việc làm không tin kính mà họ đã làm cách không tin kính, và về mọi lời cay nghiệt mà những kẻ tội lỗi không tin kính đã nói nghịch lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.B: Hê-nóc, người thứ bảy trong dòng dõi từ A-đam, cũng đã nói tiên tri về những người này. Ông nói: "Kìa! Chúa đang đến với muôn vạn đấng thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} \v 15 để phán xét mọi người, và để chứng minh mọi kẻ không tin kính là có tội về mọi việc không tin kính họ đã làm trong sự không tin kính của mình, và về mọi lời cay nghiệt mà những kẻ tội lỗi không tin kính đã nói nghịch lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.R: Hê-nóc là người thứ bảy trong dòng họ bắt đầu từ A-đam. Ông cũng đã nói một lời tiên tri về những người này. Ông nói: "Hãy xem! Chúa sẽ đến với hàng ngàn hàng vạn thiên sứ thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 15 Ngài sẽ phán xét mọi người. Ngài sẽ cho thấy mọi kẻ không tin kính đều có tội về mọi điều không tin kính họ đã làm. Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ cho thấy họ có tội về mọi lời cay nghiệt và độc ác mà những kẻ tội lỗi không tin kính đã nói nghịch lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."

pt.L: E também Enoque, o sétimo a partir de Adão, profetizou a respeito destes, dizendo: "Vejam, [o] Senhor veio com as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} santas miríades, \v 15 para executar julgamento contra todos e provar a culpa de todos os ímpios a respeito de todas as suas obras de impiedade que praticaram impiamente, e a respeito de todas as [palavras] duras que pecadores ímpios falaram contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}."
pt.B: Enoque, o sétimo na linhagem de Adão, também profetizou a respeito dessas pessoas. Ele disse: "Vejam! O Senhor está vindo com dezenas de milhares dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} santos \v 15 para julgar todos e para provar a culpa de todos os ímpios por todas as obras ímpias que praticaram na sua impiedade e por todas as palavras duras que pecadores ímpios disseram contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}."
pt.R: Enoque foi o sétimo na linhagem da família que começou com Adão. Ele também falou uma profecia a respeito dessas pessoas. Ele disse: "Vejam! O Senhor vai chegar com muitos milhares dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} santos anjos. \v 15 Ele vai julgar todos. Vai mostrar que todos os ímpios são culpados de todas as coisas ímpias que fizeram. E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai mostrar que eles são culpados de todas as palavras duras e cruéis que pecadores ímpios disseram contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}."

am.L: ከአዳም ጀምሮ ሰባተኛ የሆነው ሄኖክም ስለ እነዚህ እንዲህ ብሎ ትንቢት ተናገረ፦ «እነሆ፣ ጌታ ከቅዱሳን አእላፋቱ ጋር መጣ፤ \v 15 በሁሉ ላይ ፍርድ ሊያደርግ፣ እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩትንም ሁሉ እግዚአብሔርን ሳይፈሩ ስለ ሠሩት እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈራ ሥራቸው ሁሉ፣ እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩ ኃጢአተኞችም በእርሱ ላይ ስለ ተናገሩት ጨካኝ ቃል ሁሉ ሊወቅሳቸው።»
am.B: ከአዳም ጀምሮ ሰባተኛው ትውልድ የሆነው ሄኖክ ደግሞ ስለ እነዚህ ሰዎች ትንቢት ተናገረ። እንዲህ አለ፦ «ተመልከቱ! ጌታ ከአሥር ሺዎች ቅዱሳኑ ጋር ይመጣል፤ \v 15 ይህም በሁሉም ላይ ሊፈርድና እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩትን ሁሉ እግዚአብሔርን ሳይፈሩ ስለ ሠሩት ሥራ ሁሉ፣ እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩ ኃጢአተኞችም በእርሱ ላይ ስለ ተናገሩት ጨካኝ ቃል ሁሉ ጥፋተኞች መሆናቸውን ሊያረጋግጥ ነው።»
am.R: ሄኖክ ከአዳም ጀምሮ በተቆጠረው የቤተሰብ መስመር ሰባተኛው ሰው ነበረ። እርሱም ስለ እነዚህ ሰዎች ትንቢት ተናገረ። እንዲህ አለ፦ «እዩ! ጌታ ከብዙ ሺህ ቅዱሳን መላእክቱ ጋር ይመጣል። \v 15 በሁሉም ላይ ይፈርዳል። እግዚአብሔርን የማያከብሩ ሁሉ እግዚአብሔርን ሳያከብሩ በሠሩት ሥራ ሁሉ ጥፋተኞች መሆናቸውን ያሳያል። እግዚአብሔርን የማያከብሩ ኃጢአተኞች በእርሱ ላይ በተናገሩት ክፉና ጨካኝ ቃል ሁሉ ጥፋተኞች መሆናቸውንም ያሳያል።»

decisions.choice: Enoch, the seventh from Adam: the Enoch of Genesis 5, seventh in the line from Adam, counting Adam as the first
decisions.reason: Genesis 5:3-24 gives the line Adam, Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch: counting Adam, Enoch is the seventh. Genesis 5:24 says that Enoch walked with God, and then he was not there, because God took him. The description also keeps him distinct from Cain's son Enoch (Genesis 4:17). 1 Enoch 60:8 calls him "the seventh from Adam" in the same way.

decisions.choice: a quotation of 1 Enoch 1:9
decisions.reason: Jude's words are a close quotation of 1 Enoch 1:9. 1 Enoch is a Jewish writing, made up of several parts written in the last centuries before Christ, that tells of visions given to Enoch. It is not in the Hebrew Bible, nor in the Old Testament of most Christian churches, though the Ethiopian Orthodox Church includes it in its canon. It survives complete only in Ge'ez, the classical language of Ethiopia; parts survive in Greek, and fragments in Aramaic were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls. Jude says that Enoch prophesied, and he applies the prophecy to the false teachers. The text says nothing about the status of the book as a whole: it does not call it Scripture, and it does not say that it is not.

decisions.choice: came: a past tense used in prophecy for a future event, seen as already certain
decisions.reason: ἦλθεν is an aorist, normally a past tense. In a prophecy it presents the coming judgment as if it had already happened, because it is certain, as "they perished" does in verse 11. From Enoch's day it lay in the future, and from Jude's it is still to come.

decisions.choice: the Lord: in 1 Enoch, God; as Jude uses the prophecy, quite possibly the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: In 1 Enoch the one who comes with his holy ones is God himself, "the Holy Great One" (1 Enoch 1:3-9). Jude's quotation names him κύριος, "Lord". Jude uses that title for Jesus (verses 4, 17, 21, 25), and the New Testament speaks of the Lord Jesus coming with his holy ones (1 Thessalonians 3:13; Matthew 25:31), so Jude may apply the prophecy to him; but "Lord" is also used of God (verse 9), and the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: his holy myriads: tens of thousands of holy ones, his angels
decisions.reason: μυριάσιν means ten thousands, a countless host. The holy ones are the angels who come with the Lord at his judgment (Deuteronomy 33:2; Zechariah 14:5; Matthew 25:31).

decisions.choice: convict: prove guilty and expose; the repeated "ungodly" is the point of the prophecy
decisions.reason: ἐλέγχω means to prove someone guilty and expose their wrong. The prophecy uses the word for ungodliness four times: the ungodly, their works of ungodliness, which they did in ungodliness, ungodly sinners. The repetition is the point: their whole life is set against God. "Hard things" (σκληρῶν) are harsh, defiant words spoken against God, which verse 16 goes on to describe.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "all the ungodly"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads πάντας τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς, "all the ungodly". Some early manuscripts, among them the papyrus P72 and Codex Sinaiticus, read "every soul" instead. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: came (L); is coming (B); will come (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the past tense; Balanced and Readable say what it means here, a sure future event (m3). All three describe the same coming.

decisions.choice: Look
decisions.reason: The style guide does not use "behold". "Look" calls for attention as the Greek word does.

decisions.choice: tens of thousands of his holy ones (B); many thousands of his holy angels (R)
decisions.reason: "Myriads" is not everyday English. Readable says who the holy ones are (m5).

decisions.choice: ungodly
alternatives: people who do not honor God
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Readable explains "ungodly" (verse 4), but here the word is repeated four times on purpose (m6), so Readable keeps it.

decisions.choice: the seventh in line from Adam (B); the seventh in the family line that began with Adam (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the number counts generations (m1).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}
decisions.reason: Ἰδοὺ calls hearers to look. Spanish says it with a plural imperative, so it takes the ustedes/vosotros setting like every other plural form in the letter. "He aquí" is the older Bible form and is no longer spoken.

decisions.choice: wasiomcha Mungu / kutomcha Mungu (all levels)
decisions.reason: The prophecy repeats the word for ungodliness four times on purpose (m6), so Swahili keeps the same phrase each time, at every level, as the English Readable keeps "ungodly" here. "Wasiomcha Mungu" is the phrase used for the ungodly in 2 Peter 2-3 and in verse 4.

decisions.choice: Hénoch; Voici (L, B), Regardez (R); impie, impiété at every level
decisions.reason: "Hénoch" is the usual French form of the name. "Voici" is ordinary French for a call to attention, not an archaism like English "behold". The repeated "impie" (m6) is kept four times at every level, as the English keeps "ungodly".

decisions.choice: the quotation in 해라체, with the honorific for the Lord; "오셨다" (L), "오신다" (B), "오실 것이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The quotation of 1 Enoch 1:9 (meaning decision, footnoted) is in the 해라체 used for quoted Scripture and prophecy in the Korean letters. The past tense is prophecy of a future event seen as certain (meaning decision): Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable say it as coming.

decisions.choice: "경건하지 않은" repeated (L, B); "하나님을 공경하지 않는" (R)
decisions.reason: The repeated "ungodly" is the point of the prophecy (meaning decision), so every level repeats one Korean phrase. "경건" is the word kept for godliness, as in 2 Peter; Readable says what it means, as in 1 Peter 4:18.

decisions.choice: "아담의 칠 대손 에녹" (L, B); "아담에서 시작된 집안의 일곱째 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: Enoch is seventh in the line from Adam, counting Adam as the first (meaning decision); "칠 대손" is the plain current way of counting generations.

decisions.choice: "đã đến" (L); "đang đến" (B); "sẽ đến" (R) for "came"
decisions.reason: The prophecy uses a past tense for a future event seen as already certain (m3). Literal keeps the past with "đã", as the English Literal keeps "came"; Balanced and Readable give its meaning, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "không tin kính" repeated four times at every level
decisions.reason: The repeated "ungodly" is the point of the prophecy (m6), so Vietnamese repeats the word of 2 Peter for godliness in its negative form every time, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Hê-nóc", "A-đam"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms of the names.

decisions.choice: provar a culpa de (L, B); mostrar que ... são culpados (R)
decisions.reason: In current Brazilian Portuguese "convencer" means to persuade, not to prove guilty (m6). The name is Enoque, the Brazilian form; Readable keeps "ímpios", as the English keeps "ungodly" for the repeated word.

decisions.choice: ሄኖክ (Enoch); እነሆ (L), ተመልከቱ (B), እዩ (R) for "Look"; መጣ (came, L), ይመጣል (is coming, will come, B, R)
decisions.reason: The words are a quotation of 1 Enoch 1:9 (meaning decision m2), a book many readers of this Amharic know: the Book of Enoch (መጽሐፈ ሄኖክ) is part of the Ethiopian Orthodox Bible and has come down whole in Ge'ez. The Amharic is drafted from Jude's Greek, not from the Ge'ez book. Literal keeps the prophetic past tense (m3), and Balanced and Readable say it as future, as the English does. "እነሆ" is kept at Literal only, as the style guide settles.

decisions.choice: the fourfold "ungodly" kept: እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈሩ ... ሳይፈሩ ... የማይፈራ ... የማይፈሩ (L, B); የማያከብሩ ... ሳያከብሩ (R)
decisions.reason: The repeated word is the point of the prophecy (meaning decision m6), so every level keeps it, even where Amharic would usually avoid saying it again.

source.text: οὗτοί εἰσιν γογγυσταί, μεμψίμοιροι, κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πορευόμενοι, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν λαλεῖ ὑπέρογκα, θαυμάζοντες πρόσωπα ὠφελείας χάριν.

records.literal_gloss: These are grumblers, complainers about [their] lot, according to the desires of them going, and the mouth of them speaks swollen [things], admiring faces of advantage for the sake.

en.L: These are grumblers, complaining about their lot, going according to their desires; and their mouth speaks swollen [words], admiring faces for the sake of advantage.
en.B: These people grumble and find fault with their lot in life. They live by their own desires. Their mouths speak big, boastful words, and they flatter people to get something out of them.
en.R: These people are always grumbling and complaining that life is not fair to them. They do whatever they want. They brag with big words. And they flatter people to get what they want from them.

es.L: Estos son murmuradores, quejosos de su suerte, que andan según sus deseos; y su boca habla [palabras] infladas, admirando rostros por causa de provecho.
es.B: Estas personas murmuran y se quejan de su suerte. Viven según sus propios deseos. Su boca dice palabras grandes y arrogantes, y adulan a la gente para sacar provecho.
es.R: Estas personas siempre están murmurando y quejándose de que la vida no les da lo que merecen. Hacen lo que les da la gana. Se jactan con palabras grandes. Y adulan a la gente para conseguir de ella lo que quieren.

sw.L: Hawa ni wanung'unikaji, walalamikaji juu ya fungu lao, wakienenda kwa kufuata tamaa zao; na kinywa chao kinanena [maneno] yaliyovimba, wakistaajabia nyuso kwa ajili ya faida.
sw.B: Watu hawa wananung'unika na kulalamikia fungu lao maishani. Wanaishi kwa kufuata tamaa zao wenyewe. Vinywa vyao vinasema maneno makubwa ya kujivuna, nao wanawabembeleza watu ili wapate faida kutoka kwao.
sw.R: Watu hawa daima wananung'unika na kulalamika kwamba wamepunjwa maishani. Wanafanya lolote wanalotaka. Wanajisifu kwa maneno makubwa. Tena wanawabembeleza watu ili wapate wanachotaka kutoka kwao.

fr.L: Ce sont des murmurateurs, mécontents de leur sort, allant selon leurs désirs ; et leur bouche prononce des [paroles] enflées, admirant les visages en vue d’un profit.
fr.B: Ces gens murmurent et se plaignent de leur sort. Ils vivent selon leurs propres désirs. Leur bouche prononce de grands mots pleins d’orgueil, et ils flattent les gens pour en tirer profit.
fr.R: Ces gens sont toujours en train de murmurer et de se plaindre que la vie n’est pas juste pour eux. Ils font tout ce qu’ils veulent. Ils se vantent avec de grands mots. Et ils flattent les gens pour obtenir d’eux ce qu’ils veulent.

ko.L: 이 사람들은 불평하는 사람들이요, 자기 처지를 원망하는 사람들이며, 자기들의 욕망대로 살아갑니다. 그들의 입은 과장된 말을 하고, 이익을 얻으려고 사람의 얼굴을 우러러봅니다.
ko.B: 이 사람들은 불평하고, 자기 처지에 대해 늘 원망합니다. 그들은 자기 욕망대로 삽니다. 그들의 입은 허풍을 떨고, 무엇인가 얻어 내려고 사람들에게 아첨합니다.
ko.R: 이 사람들은 늘 불평하고, 인생이 자기들에게 공평하지 않다고 투덜거립니다. 그들은 자기 하고 싶은 대로 합니다. 그들은 큰소리로 자랑합니다. 그리고 원하는 것을 얻어 내려고 사람들에게 아첨합니다.

vi.L: Những kẻ này là những kẻ hay lằm bằm, than phiền về số phận mình, sống theo dục vọng riêng; miệng họ nói những lời khoa trương, và vì lợi lộc mà nịnh hót người ta.
vi.B: Những người này hay lằm bằm và bất mãn với số phận mình. Họ sống theo dục vọng riêng. Miệng họ nói những lời khoe khoang to tát, và họ nịnh hót người khác để trục lợi.
vi.R: Những người này lúc nào cũng lằm bằm và phàn nàn rằng đời đối xử không công bằng với mình. Họ muốn gì làm nấy. Họ khoe khoang bằng những lời to tát. Và họ nịnh hót người ta để có được điều mình muốn.

pt.L: Estes são murmuradores, queixosos da [sua] sorte, andando segundo os seus desejos; e a boca deles fala [palavras] inchadas, admirando rostos por causa de vantagem.
pt.B: Essas pessoas vivem murmurando e reclamando da sua sorte na vida. Vivem segundo os próprios desejos. A boca delas fala palavras grandiosas e arrogantes, e elas bajulam os outros para tirar proveito deles.
pt.R: Essas pessoas estão sempre murmurando e reclamando que a vida não é justa com elas. Fazem tudo o que querem. Elas se gabam com palavras grandiosas. E bajulam os outros para conseguir deles o que querem.

am.L: እነዚህ የሚያጉረመርሙ፣ በዕጣቸው የሚያማርሩ፣ እንደ ምኞታቸው የሚመላለሱ ናቸው፤ አፋቸውም የተጋነነ ትዕቢትን ይናገራል፤ ለጥቅም ሲሉ ፊትን ያደንቃሉ።
am.B: እነዚህ ሰዎች ያጉረመርማሉ፤ በዕጣቸውም ያማርራሉ። በገዛ ምኞታቸው ይመራሉ። አፋቸው የትዕቢትና የጉራ ቃል ይናገራል፤ ከሰዎች አንዳች ለማግኘትም ይሸነግላሉ።
am.R: እነዚህ ሰዎች ሁልጊዜ ያጉረመርማሉ፤ ሕይወት ፍትሕ አልሰጠንም እያሉ ያማርራሉ። የፈለጉትን ሁሉ ያደርጋሉ። በትልቅ ቃል ጉራ ይነዛሉ። ከሰዎች የሚፈልጉትን ለማግኘት ይሸነግሏቸዋል።

decisions.choice: grumblers: like Israel in the wilderness
decisions.reason: γογγυσταί recalls Israel's grumbling against God and Moses in the wilderness (Exodus 16:7-12; Numbers 14:27-29), which ended in the judgment of verse 5. Paul uses the same example (1 Corinthians 10:10).

decisions.choice: complaining about their lot: discontented with what God has given them
decisions.reason: μεμψίμοιροι describes someone who finds fault with his share in life. Their complaint is finally against God, who gives each person a lot.

decisions.choice: swollen words: boastful, arrogant talk
decisions.reason: ὑπέρογκα means puffed up, swollen beyond its size. 2 Peter 2:18 uses it of the false teachers' empty talk, and Daniel 11:36 says that the arrogant king will speak great things against God.

decisions.choice: admiring faces for the sake of advantage: flattering people who can benefit them
decisions.reason: θαυμάζοντες πρόσωπα, "admiring faces", is a Greek form of a Hebrew way of speaking of partiality, "lifting up the face" of someone, which the Law forbids in judgment (Leviticus 19:15; Deuteronomy 10:17; compare James 2:1-9). ὠφελείας χάριν, "for the sake of advantage": they flatter those who can do something for them.

decisions.choice: flatter people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means here (m4).

decisions.choice: big, boastful words (B); brag with big words (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Peter 2:18 (m3).

decisions.choice: "사람의 얼굴을 우러러봅니다" (L); "아첨합니다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Admiring faces" is a Hebrew way of saying "flattering people who can benefit them" (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture of the face, and Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: ያጉረመርማሉ (grumble), the word for Israel's grumbling in the wilderness; ፊትን ያደንቃሉ (admire faces, L), ይሸነግላሉ (flatter, B, R)
decisions.reason: "ማጉረምረም" is the Amharic word for the grumbling of Israel in the wilderness (meaning decision m1), so the echo can be heard. Literal keeps the Greek idiom "admire faces"; Balanced and Readable say what it means, flattering people for gain (m4).

records.literal_gloss: You but, beloved, remember the words the having been spoken beforehand by the apostles of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, \v 18 that they were saying to you: In [the] last time will be scoffers, according to the of themselves desires going of the ungodlinesses.

en.L: But you, beloved, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 18 that they were saying to you, "In [the] final time there will be scoffers, going according to their own desires for ungodly things."
en.B: But you, dear friends, must remember the words spoken in advance by the apostles of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 18 They used to tell you, "In the last time, scoffers will come, driven by their own ungodly desires."
en.R: But you, dear friends, must remember what the apostles of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} told you would happen. \v 18 They used to tell you, "In the last time, people will come who laugh and sneer. They will live by their own ungodly desires."

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, amados, {{plural_you:acuérdense|acordaos}} de las palabras dichas de antemano por los apóstoles de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, \v 18 que {{plural_you:les|os}} decían: «En [el] último tiempo habrá burladores, que andarán según sus propios deseos de impiedades».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, queridos, {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} recordar las palabras que dijeron de antemano los apóstoles de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. \v 18 Ellos {{plural_you:les|os}} decían: «En el último tiempo vendrán burladores, llevados por sus propios deseos impíos».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, queridos amigos, {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} recordar lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciaron los apóstoles de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. \v 18 Ellos {{plural_you:les|os}} decían: «En el último tiempo vendrá gente que se ríe y se burla. Vivirán según sus propios deseos impíos».

sw.B: Lakini ninyi, wapendwa, yakumbukeni maneno yaliyosemwa mapema na mitume wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 18 Walikuwa wakiwaambia, "Katika wakati wa mwisho watakuja wadhihaki, wakiongozwa na tamaa zao wenyewe za kutomcha Mungu."

fr.B: Mais vous, mes chers amis, souvenez-vous des paroles que les apôtres de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} ont dites à l’avance. \v 18 Ils vous disaient : « Dans le dernier temps, il viendra des moqueurs, menés par leurs propres désirs impies. »
fr.R: Mais vous, mes chers amis, souvenez-vous de ce que les apôtres de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} vous ont annoncé. \v 18 Ils vous disaient : « Dans le dernier temps, des gens viendront qui se moqueront de tout et ricaneront. Ils vivront selon leurs propres désirs impies. »

ko.L: 그러나 사랑하는 여러분, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 사도들이 미리 한 말씀들을 기억하십시오. \v 18 그들은 여러분에게 "마지막 때에 자기들의 경건하지 않은 욕망대로 사는 조롱하는 사람들이 있을 것이다" 하고 말했습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 사랑하는 여러분, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 사도들이 미리 한 말씀을 꼭 기억하십시오. \v 18 그들은 여러분에게 "마지막 때에 비웃는 사람들이 나타나서 자기들의 경건하지 않은 욕망대로 살 것이다" 하고 늘 말했습니다.

vi.B: Nhưng thưa anh chị em yêu dấu, phải nhớ lại những lời các sứ đồ của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} đã nói trước. \v 18 Họ thường nói với anh chị em: "Vào thời kỳ cuối cùng, sẽ có những kẻ chế giễu đến, bị dục vọng không tin kính của chính mình dẫn dắt."
vi.R: Nhưng anh chị em thân mến, phải nhớ những gì các sứ đồ của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} đã nói trước với anh chị em. \v 18 Các sứ đồ thường nói với anh chị em: "Vào thời kỳ cuối cùng, sẽ có những người đến cười nhạo và chế giễu.
